News.title: What did love-in between Burnham and Macron ACTUALLY achieve? Don’t expect migrant crossings to stop for a start
News.content:
French folly

WHAT did yesterday’s love-in between Andy Burnham and Emmanuel Macron actually achieve?

For a start, don’t expect the small boats to stop any time soon.



It’s still hugely in France’s interest to let migrants set sail and wait for British border forces to rescue them – especially as we pay £1billion for the privilege.

Burnham’s welcoming of a measly 45 extra officers to patrol hundreds of miles of northern French coastline shows the Government is still pathetically grateful for minimum French support.



Yesterday, he couldn’t help gushing over France’s role in another terrible idea: helping him achieve closer ties to the EU. Sir Keir Starmer was conned by Macron into huge giveaways as part of his notorious “reset”.

That included meekly taking rules and standards on food and energy and agreeing to a “youth mobility” scheme for EU workers under 30.

After the summit it seems we must now prepare for further betrayals of Brexit by Burnham.

But if he thinks binding Britain to the EU is the answer, the PM must be even more confused about economic reality than we thought.

Even Britain’s flat-lining economy has outperformed France, Germany and other European nations since Brexit.

Precious few “postcodes” across the EU have seen any growth.



How would further cosying up to Brussels help Burnham deliver it here?

Indefensible

HOW much more damage can Labour’s dithering over defence spending inflict?

Never mind actually fighting the Russians in a real war.

As we reveal today, Army top brass are now so cash-strapped they can’t even afford for soldiers to PRACTISE.

Forcing the axe of major war games with immediate effect is unprecedented.



It is a terrifying example of the decline forced on our military by useless politicians who care more about delivering the next welfare cheque than protecting the country from Vladimir Putin.

Last night, Argentinian president Javier Milei used a nationwide TV address to tell his people they have a “sacred right” to the Falkland Islands.

What chance would Britain have of defending them now?

Loss of Power

THE grim news that Paddy Power could shut 100 high street shops is proof of the insanity of this Government’s war on fun.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Around 400 jobs are now at risk, adding to those suffered in closures already announced by William Hill and Betfred.



Labour’s senseless taxes and intrusive affordability checks are sending regulated firms to the wall while driving punters into the arms of online black market gangs.

News.title: I’ll declare a national emergency on my first day as PM & sack any minister who fails to deliver, Nigel Farage will vow
News.content:
REFORM UK leader Nigel Farage will today pledge to declare a “national emergency” on his first day as PM.

He will also vow to sack any minister who fails to deliver.



In his conference speech, Mr Farage plans to tell party activists that MPs should “sit day and night” to crash through urgent laws and fight civil service resistance.

He aims to use the speech as a reset following Reform’s dip in the polls.



Mr Farage has been dogged by questions about an undeclared £5million gift and is facing a Commons probe.

The Brexiteer will use his opening address to prove he is still focused on becoming PM and has a plan for No10.



He will say: “Within days of winning the general election, we will introduce dozens of bills and force Parliament to sit all through summer for seven days a week to pass them.

“Britain is in serious trouble. We don’t have time to wait around to fix it”.

Key issues for the would-be PM are the illegal migration crisis and the cost of living.

He would compel Parliament to sit round-the-clock and even through the summer holidays should he win power.



Anticipating pushback from the Whitehall machine, he will say: “If the Lords, judiciary or civil service get in our way they will discover just how determined we are” and will commit to doing “anything and everything to make the first 100 days work”.

And he will warn any ministers who fail to get on top of their brief have “no place in my cabinet”.

Reform is tied at 23 per cent with Andy Burnham’s Labour after surrendering their 15-month lead, according to a “poll of polls”.

One recent survey even had Mr Farage dipping below Kemi Badenoch’s Tory party.

But despite the setbacks, he will insist the party was “much stronger than we were last year” and add: “I believe that Reform can win it.”



Mr Farage won the Clacton by-election he himself triggered to win the judgement of his constituents over the £5million gift scandal.

He could be forced to fight another contest should he be sanctioned by Parliament’s Standards Commissioner.

News.title: Plan to send just 45 extra French cops on to beaches to stop small boats slammed as ‘next to useless’
News.content:
FORTY-FIVE French cops have been branded “next to useless” as they will not have powers to enter the water to tackle small boat crossings.

A new “surge team” will patrol along the country’s coastline targeting criminal gangs launching mega-dinghies – carrying up to 230 migrants.



The officers will need special permission from their commander to enter the water once the boats are launched, based on operational decisions at the time.

However, they are only expected to receive the green light if there is an immediate threat to life.



Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp said: “It’s a joke these officers can’t even go into knee-deep water to stop illegal immigrants. This will mean they’re next to useless.

“More officers changes nothing if they are still banned from going into the water, because once a dinghy has launched they can only stand on the beach and watch it leave.

“I saw this for myself in France recently with ten armed French Gendarmes Nationale – who UK taxpayers fund – standing around doing nothing while 100 illegal immigrants embarked in knee deep water.

“The £660 million we pay should be withheld until the French prevent all embarkations in shallow waters.”

The revelation comes as Andy Burnham met with French President Emmanuel Macron in Downing Street yesterday with the issue a focal point of talks.

The Sun warned the Prime Minister to avoid a stitch-up by the French in its front page yesterday as the Bayeux Tapestry was viewed by the two leaders on the visit.



The new surge team will be made up of both gendarmes and reservists from the Police Nationale. There are more than 1,000 patrolling beaches in the region.

There are currently 125 officers who are allowed to step in and stop boats in the water.

Launches of the mega-dinghies are taking place more than 100 miles away from Calais as the authorities crack down on the perilous journeys on more western beaches in Normandy.



France says it’s now stopping 60 per cent of all the dinghies launched but interceptions of migrants stands at just 34 per cent.

A concern for officials on both sides of the Channel is the average number of people per dinghy now stands at 80 people.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has defended French cops amid criticism over officers failing to stop packed dinghies once they reach the water.

She said French officers have “much fewer options” at the water’s edge because of the risk to migrants’ lives.

Ms Mahmood said: “If you only look at activity that’s happening at the water’s edge, actually that’s the last point at which anything can be done because at that point you’ve got an operational risk of people being in the water, and then obviously French officials have to make a decision based on operational risk to life.



“If you just go a few 100 yards up from water’s edge, you will see a lot of disruption activity.

“There is a huge amount of work happening with French law enforcement that is literally stopping people from actually getting to water’s edge in the first place.”

Downing Street said that both Mr Burnham and his counterpart have agreed to “step up work across the full spectrum” of shared challenges.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A spokesman said “operational teams were making headway on driving down numbers and reducing crossings”

They added: “It was now vital to ensure that success was scaled up across Europe to deter illegal migration, the leaders agreed.”

News.title: UK’s biggest danger is delusional group sitting behind Burnham… they’d rather spend on welfare than keeping nation safe
News.content:
WITH all the talk of funding Britain’s defences in the face of an imminent threat from Russia, you might be forgiven for thinking that Vladimir Putin is the biggest menace to our national security.

But you’d be wrong. And, no, it isn’t China, Iran or Islamist terrorists either.



The greatest danger to our nation’s defences is actually the group of people sitting behind Prime Minister Andy Burnham on the green leather benches in the House of Commons.

I am, of course, talking about Labour’s 403 MPs.



It is the ranks of Labour MPs — both on the backbenches and those serving in the Government, including Andy Burnham himself — who are the real threat because it is they who are preventing us from being able to defend ourselves.

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch has this week joined the Reform leader Nigel Farage in pledging to raise spending on defence to three per cent of GDP by 2030 — all funded by slashing welfare spending.

Yet the man who is sitting in Downing Street with the power to deliver that promise right now is point blank refusing to make that vow.

Even more astonishingly, so is his Chancellor John Healey, who resigned as Defence Secretary just a few short months ago because he claimed that budget boost was vital to keep Britain safe.

Why? Because Labour would rather spend billions on welfare for millions of people who don’t need it than keep the entire nation secure.

This, after all, is the same bunch of lefties who voted down an attempt by Sir Keir Starmer to cut the planned increase in the welfare bill by just £5billion to free up some extra cash.



Instead of funding our military properly, we have created an army of mental health malingerers living on benefits whose votes are crucial to the Labour MPs who want to keep their own well-paid jobs in Parliament, and who believe that cutting welfare to boost defence spending is not only the wrong thing to do, it’s immoral and cruel.

Even if failing to deter the threat from Russia means we are far more likely to end up having to go to war, which would cost many, many thousands of lives.

That’s the real problem. We have a huge majority in Parliament for an entire party that just doesn’t accept reality.

We have hundreds of Labour MPs who think that taxing people more and spending more public money will deliver growth, who insist that men can magically become women, who genuinely fear that we’re all about to die in a climate change catastrophe, and who really do believe that the people who don’t want a free-for-all for any foreign criminal to come to our shores are all far-right fascists.

They are dangerously delusional. They are fantasists, living in a left-wing la-la land of their own hysterical imaginations.



When it comes to the very real threats facing our nation, they bury their heads in the sand.

Whether it’s illegal migrants raping women and girls, or the madness of Net Zero’s stranglehold on our economy, or the menace of Putin’s Russia, they simply shrug their shoulders, sip on their almond milk lattes and pretend it’s not happening.

Despite years of increasingly frantic warnings from military chiefs and Nato allies about the threat from Russia, most Labour MPs — like our most recent and current PM — won’t do anything but pay lip service to the defence of the realm.



There are a few honourable exceptions on Labour’s benches, such as Tan Dhesi, the chairman of the Commons Defence Committee, who has argued that more investment is “imperative”, warning that, with Trump’s waning interest in European security, Burnham’s “vibes” weren’t going to be enough to keep us safe.

Yet his fellow Labour MP Diane Abbott insisted this week that the Russian threat was “Nato fiction” made up to justify giving in to Donald Trump’s demands for more defence spending.

Tell that to the Ukrainians burying their war dead for the last four years.

Then there’s the latest sabre-rattling from Argentine President Javier Milei over his bid to claim the Falkland Islands 44 years after his country’s invasion of the sovereign British territory.

Could we even defend our fellow Brits if Milei did the same?



Spending more on defence isn’t an optional extra.

It’s a necessity. In fact, even boosting our defence spending to three per cent of our national income is only the bare minimum we need to commit.

Britain is spending just 2.3 per cent of GDP — that’s £68billion — on defence this year.

An increase to three per cent by 2030, given current growth forecasts, would mean spending £108billion on our military that year, with a Nato pledge to spend even more to reach 3.5 per cent by 2035.

But in all likelihood, we could already be spending ten times that by 2035 if we are already at war.



It’s not just dangerous to fail to boost defence spending. It’s immoral.

If we do not have the military forces and equipment to defeat our enemies if they want to attack us, then we cannot deter that attack. And that puts British lives at risk.

Spending money on defence is the best way — the only way — to avoid war.

If Labour MPs don’t face up to reality soon, the cost to our nation will be a far heavier price to pay.

TEMPTED BY 2-FOR-1 DEAL, DON?



AT least someone is happy that Prince Harry and Meghan have moved back to Britain.

That someone is Donald Trump, who’s said he was glad to see the back of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex.

“I was not a fan”, he said of the Duchess, who was “disrespectful” to the late Queen and King Charles.

I’m wondering if we’re missing a trick here, now that Sir Keir Starmer has decided to end his political career with one last U-turn (by resigning as an MP when he said he wouldn’t) to, he says, focus on “international affairs”.

I’m not sure what the rest of the world has done to deserve Starmer’s attentions, but since we don’t want him any more, why don’t we create a new US version of Starmer’s one-in, one-out deal with France to return Channel migrants.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

We’ve taken back two unwanted migrants to America so it’s only fair that, in return, we should ask President Trump if he will offer safe refuge to just one used ex-Prime Minister (nearly new, one careful former national owner and a huge life-long pension).

For the man who wrote “The Art Of The Deal”, this two-for-one offer is the bargain of the century.

News.title: Deeply troubled mum or cold-blooded murderer? How Lindsay Clancy’s trial has gripped America – so what would you decide?
News.content:
IT sounds like it should be a simple guilty verdict.

A mother waited for her husband to leave and run errands, then violently strangled her three children with exercise bands.



Instead, five weeks into the extraordinary trial of former nurse Lindsay Clancy, the jury — made up of nine women and three men — are still in deadlock after six days of deliberation.

Outside the courtroom and across the internet, Lindsay’s supporters are pleading for them to find the former midwife innocent of three counts of first-degree murder.



Here in Massachusetts where the trial is taking place, the streets are lined with her supporters.

Many are mothers themselves — dressed in pink tops with slogans such as “She Needed Help” and “Peace For Lindsay” to show her they are on her side.

Parents have taken their kids out of school to stand outside the courthouse in “solidarity” with Lindsay.

One mum rowed with another mother on the opposite side.

Some people have ditched work to livestream from the outside the courthouse.

One told us: “I started with 2,000 followers, now I have 20,000.”



It is a case that has gripped America since 2023 when Lindsay, 36, admitted killing Cora, five, Dawson, three, and baby Callan in the basement of their family home on January 24 that year.

The troubled mother then slashed her wrists and neck and threw herself out of a second-storey window, leaving her paralysed from the waist down.

The prosecution argues Lindsay made a calculated, intentional decision to kill her three small children.



But her lawyer says she was suffering from postpartum psychosis at the time, and therefore could not distinguish right from wrong.

The case has become an internet sensation with amateur sleuths and armchair detectives turning the trial into whodunit content, dissecting every detail and advancing theories across TikTok.

Clancy’s lawyer, Kevin Reddington, has become an unlikely hero to her supporters who say he is fighting for every mother that has been in crisis.



If convicted, Lindsay faces a potential life sentence without parole.

If she is found not guilty by reason of insanity, she would be committed to a mental health hospital with reviews to determine if she could safely be released.

But as the case continues to divide not just America but the world, what would you decide?

Here, we lay out the arguments from both sides.

THE PROSECUTION



Prosecutors say Lindsay was a “functioning mum” who meticulously planned the murder of her three young children inside their suburban home.

They do not dispute that she had mental health problems and tried to end her life, but they question her mental state at the time of the killings.

In court, they argued that she plotted the murders ahead of time and acted with intention, which indicates she was not psychotic.

Prosecutors say Lindsay contrived to get her then-husband Patrick out of the house by sending him to get a takeaway and to the pharmacy before choking her kids with exercise bands.



It was discussed how she was looking up how long it would take her ex-husband to get to the restaurant and back, which they maintain was to ensure she had enough time to execute the killings.

Patrick then called her to find out what medication he should be getting and she did not answer.

She then phoned him back and the call lasted 14 seconds.

The defence says the voices in Lindsay’s head and the killings did not start until after Patrick called her.

But, as the prosecution says, that is not enough time to murder her three children and try to kill herself.



They asserted that Lindsay must have begun carrying out the killings immediately after her husband left home, disputing her claim that she killed her children in just under 20 minutes.

They also put forward an argument that her Apple Watch recorded her climbing flights of stairs three times, including after the call.

Her critics say this proves she rang Patrick back after she killed her children as she was not recorded coming back downstairs.

The state also cast doubt on the defence’s accounts of hallucinations, pointing out that medical records indicate Lindsay did not report hearing voices until after her children’s deaths.

One of her psychiatrists testified that she did not show signs of psychosis during their sessions.



They say Lindsay was not over-medicated because few or no pills were missing from the bottles of the 13 prescription medications she was given.

And they called a doctor to the stand who disputed her account of the voices.

The doctor testified that it was unusual for the voices to stop abruptly right after the strangulation.

They noted that Lindsay never reported hearing voices to medical providers prior to the incident, and found her overall timeline unconvincing.

The prosecution argued that Lindsay’s suicide attempt was “superficial” even though she said the voice was compelling her to do it.



The drugs were not taken in high enough quantities to die, the cuts were not deep enough and the window was not high enough.

If she were truly compelled by a voice, they said, Lindsay would have succeeded.

A state police investigator described searches made on her phone days before the killings in which she sought information about schizophrenia, hallucinations and psychosis.

She also searched, “Can you treat a sociopath?”

The prosecution’s final witness was FBI psychiatrist Dr Gregory Saathoff who said that Lindsay could still appreciate right from wrong and control her behaviour when she killed her children.



He pointed to her “preparatory planning” which included conducting searches on her phone and mapping the distance from their home to a restaurant.

In their closing argument, the prosecution argued that Lindsay killed her kids as she was upset and she wanted to end her misery, but they were keeping her alive.

She therefore had to “remove the protective factor” and that it was a “choice she made”.

The prosecution is pushing for a first-degree murder conviction.

THE DEFENCE



The defendant’s legal team have never rejected her role in the choking of her three children.

Instead, they have put forth a defence of insanity, arguing that Lindsay had hallucinations and delusions after giving birth to her youngest child.

They say she killed her children after a voice told her to do it — then tried to kill herself.

Their defence hinges on her suffering from postpartum psychosis, a rare condition in which postpartum women can experience mania, depression or a mixture of both.



Lindsay’s ex-husband Patrick told the court that she had experienced anxiety after the births of their first two children.

He said her symptoms returned after their third child was born in 2022 and they intensified as she prepared to return to work.

She was then prescribed more than a dozen different medications by doctors which her lawyers argue drastically affected her mind.

Patrick said that clinicians had failed to monitor her reactions to the meds “or attend to her worsening psychiatric conditions”.

He testified that twice in December 2022 — a month before the killings — Lindsay had told him she had harboured thoughts of harming their children.



She admitted herself to an outpatient programme for postpartum depression before admitting herself to a psychiatric hospital in January 2023 where she stayed for five days.

Medical professionals testified that Lindsay had months of severe postpartum depression symptoms and said she made two calls to a suicide hotline before the killings.

A hospital chaplain said that Clancy mentioned multiple times after the killings that a persistent male voice was goading her to kill her children and herself.

Patrick claimed later that month she heard “a compelling and unrecognisable singular male voice” telling her that she “should die”.

He described seeing his son Dawson sitting on the couch eating chicken nuggets before he left the home to get medication and a takeaway.



He came back 54 minutes later to find his children dead.

Despite never being a suspect, baseless conspiracy theories have swirled online about his involvement.

Patrick has come under fire by armchair detectives for remarrying in April 2026 — just three years after the incident — and allegedly taking a holiday to Costa Rica 18 days after his children’s funeral.

Lindsay’s supporters have also criticised how supportive he was as a husband.

They argue CCTV footage shows Patrick not helping her with the kids, despite her fragile state.



They also picked holes in the timeline.

During the trial, it was testified that Lindsay was hypothermic after falling out of the window with a core body temperature of 27C when paramedics arrived.

Web detectives say that her temperature could not have been that low if she had only just thrown herself from the window, suggesting she must have been outside longer.

Patrick claims Lindsay told him that the children were in the basement when he arrived back home.

But TikTok sleuths pointed out emergency responders testified she could only mumble and moan after her suicide attempt.



Patrick also said that when he got home he tried to call 911 but he had Wi-Fi issues which sleuths say “doesn’t add up” as emergency calls do not need an internet connection.

The prosecution put forward an argument that Clancy crushed pills in her drink before trying to kill herself, which showed she was lucid.

But her defence said the medication was never tested and there was no pill crusher or residue found.

Patrick’s mother also testified that Lindsay was “begging for help” in the months before the killings and disclosed her struggle with anxiety, depression and insomnia that year.

She also described her as a warm and devoted mum.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

A former colleague testified that Lindsay was a compassionate midwife who was deeply emotional about patients’ deliveries.

Lindsay broke down several times in court when jurors were shown autopsy photos of her children.

News.title: Dangerous knife and gun criminals are being let loose on streets due to overcrowded prisons, warns Met chief
News.content:
A NOTTING Hill Carnival reveller caught with an 18-inch “sword” was back on the streets last night – the fourth time he has been freed after being caught with deadly blades this year.

Met Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley revealed the “deeply concerning” case today as he said the “overloaded justice system is getting weaker and weaker,” leaving criminals with guns and knives at large.



Sir Mark told the Met’s governing London Policing Board that tough legal curbs on firearms and knives introduced earlier this century were no longer being enforced because of the “massively stretched” justice system.

He said police “offender control” was being undermined and cited the Carnival thug caught with a huge blade by cops during the late August street festival, who was then freed by a court.



Sir Mark said the weapon was “like a small sword, about 18 inches long with a handle.”

He added of the offender: “This is his fourth knife offence this year.”



The D-handled Zombie knife was found hidden in a trouser leg of a 17-year-old boy in Ladbroke Grove on Sunday.

He was arrested and appeared in custody at Highbury Corner Magistrates’ Court on Monday and pleaded guilty to possession of a bladed article.

The teen – already on court bail – was freed again and granted conditional bail to attend Willesden Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, 1 October for sentencing.

Sir Mark said the suspect “pleaded guilty to two offences earlier and got a referral order” and then admitted a third offence a few weeks ago and was on bail pending sentence.



He added: “He’s now on bail and has two referral orders.

“He tries to take a small sword into Carnival, and he’s been bailed again.”

Sir Mark added: “That is deeply concerning to me….”

The Met chief said custodial sentences for “even key knife carriers” were “rapidly reducing,” and far fewer were being remanded in custody.

He added that cops were “seeing people charged again and again and again with carrying knives…”



Sir Mark said gun suspects were also being freed by courts, with 34 people currently charged with firearms offences and awaiting trial in London on bail.

Nine of those cases involved shots being fired, some during confrontations, he said.

Sir Mark said policing colleagues around the country had noticed the same trend with London experiencing a sharper load.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Cops were dealing with stabbings and “one or two” homicides involving offenders and suspects already in the criminal justice system, he said.

He added that the overloaded system was not going to improve soon and stressed that law enforcement had to “get much better” at dealing with the “most dangerous and most prolific.”

News.title: Fury as council collects RUBBISH from travellers ‘living illegally in plain sight’ after land grab on ‘wildlife haven’
News.content:
VILLAGERS have blasted a council for collecting bags of household rubbish from travellers living at an ­illegal land grab site.

An injunction granted four months ago bans anyone from occupying the site or carrying out any further development.



But bin lorries now include the 12-pitch site in their weekly rounds in Willows Green, Essex.

Locals plan to stage a protest tonight outside Uttlesford council’s offices in Saffron Walden.



One reckoned: “They are living there illegally in plain sight but the council has done nothing.

“To add insult to injury the travellers, who don’t pay any council tax, are getting bins collected.

“It is a complete joke. The villagers have now had enough.”

The privately-owned field, once home to great crested newts and rare albino fallow deer, was concreted over on the first May bank holiday.



Uttlesford council served a stop notice on May 5 and secured a High Court injunction days later.

Last week, travellers submitted a retrospective planning application for 12 mobile homes on the site.

Uttlesford council said it had a legal duty to collect waste.

A spokesman said: “We understand the frustration felt by local residents and remain committed to using the powers available to us to address unauthorised development.”



The row comes after two more traveller land grabs over the August bank holiday weekend on privately-owned land in Rochford, Essex, and Sawbridgeworth, Herts.

In both cases the local councils issued stop notices and sought injunctions to block further work.

News.title: Giant 46-acre ‘monstrosity’ has been built at the end of our gardens – we hear constant bangs & lost all sunlight
News.content:
BANG OUT OF ORDER Giant 46-acre ‘monstrosity’ has been built at the end of our gardens – we hear constant bangs & lost all sunlight

FAMILIES living in the shadow of a data centre have branded it a “monstrosity” after it blocked all sunlight from reaching their gardens.

Residents of Newport, South Wales, say they are woken up every morning by loud bangs coming from the building.



Dale, who has lived at a property near the site with his wife for over 20 years, said “constant bangs” can be heard from 8am to 6pm – and even on Saturdays.

The data centre is yet to officially open with Dale saying he fears what the future will look like when the site opens fully.



He said: “They are there 8am every morning. There is continuous noise from machines and they don’t finish until 6pm.

“They don’t give us a break from it all. It has made my wife ill with worry.



“We have lost the sun. We used to see it setting behind our house and now it is hidden behind the site.”

He added: “Construction is supposed to end this year. We don’t know what it will all sound like when they have all the fans running when it opens.



“I made sure they put up a wooden fence in my garden for some privacy and they planted some trees. They clean our windows once a month but that’s it.

“We have monthly meetings with Vantage but they are going to stop after Christmas and what will happen then?

“It feels like Newport City Council just rubber stamped the whole thing without thinking about the people living here.”

Neighbour Amanda Young said families living on the street are concerned about house prices being impacted.

She said: “It used to be a nice, quiet area but with more data centres coming in, we kind of don’t know what they’re going to bring with them.



“My biggest concern is the noise, the visual impact and whether it will affect house prices. Whichever window you look out, you can see it. “When you’re sitting in the lounge, you can actually see it there.”

A 79-year-old neighbour, who lives in a cottage across the street, said he used to be surrounded by agricultural land before the industrial unit was built.

He said: “I have been here 51 years. There used to be cows in the garden and I could see to Cardiff from here.



“I don’t think that it will all get used once it is built. I think everybody is throwing money at AI and nobody has stopped to think what is the long term future of it.

“Is it really going to help the people of Newport? Is it really going to stop rough sleeping or benefit people here?”

The number of data centres across the UK is on the rise following a boom in the use of artificial intelligence – and the UK government says they are critical national infrastructure.

Concerns have been raised about the resources needed to power the centres – including electricity, grid capacity and water.

It comes after campaigners have blasted plans for a data centre campus at a Park & Ride site in Llanrumney, Cardiff.



A spokesman for Vantage Data Center said they were “committed to being a good neighbour.”

They said they “work closely with local authorities to manage construction activity, including traffic, noise and lighting” as well as incorporating “measures designed to protect the local environment”.

Newport City Council said it worked to “ensure that the impacts are considered acceptable in terms of biodiversity, light, noise and construction traffic” when considering planning applications.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A Welsh government spokesman said: “Any proposed data centre development remains subject to the existing planning system and environmental regulation, with robust checks and balances in place to ensure that environmental and community impacts are properly considered before consent is granted.

“Investment in data centres has the potential to create new economic opportunities and support skilled employment, while strengthening Wales‘ attractiveness as a leading destination for advanced digital investment.”

News.title: FIFA accuse UEFA of launching 'smear campaign' against Gianni Infantino
News.content:
FIFA accuse UEFA of launching 'smear campaign' against Gianni Infantino

FIFA and UEFA's bitter public spat has taken another turn with the latter accused of launching a 'smear campaign' against Gianni Infantino following his plot to sell World Cup shares

View 2 Images Aleksandr Ceferin and Gianni Infantino do not see eye to eye (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

UEFA has been accused of running a "smear campaign" against Gianni Infantino by FIFA following the former's attempt to launch legal action over a failed plot to sell shares in the World Cup.

‌



Infantino was heavily criticised after unveiling a scheme to sell off shares in future FIFA tournaments to private investors, with UEFA's nations even threatening to boycott World Cups if the proposals were put into action.

‌



The 56-year-old eventually rowed back on the proposals but has been subjected to calls for his resignation, while it emerged last week that UEFA are preparing a criminal file against Infantino.

‌



They filed legal papers in the United States requesting the release of evidence and documents from FIFA. But they have responded with court filings of their own in which they accused UEFA of "a smear campaign against it and its leadership".

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The governing body also claims that UEFA's argument suffers from "legal deficiencies". According to BBC Sport, the filings say: "UEFA seeks discovery in aid of a foreign criminal proceeding that does not exist and that UEFA admittedly lacks the authority to initiate. Despite that threshold problem, UEFA asks this court to authorise sweeping discovery about the FFE."

‌



FIFA went on to stress that it had "made clear" the creation of FFE (Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme) was "only a proposal" and would not have proceeded without overwhelming support.

"Rather than participate in that democratic process, Uefa issued a press release - the beginning of a weeks-long smear campaign against Fifa and its leadership," FIFA wrote.

In their court filing, UEFA described the creation of FFE as "a vehicle for Infantino and a small circle to acquire a permanent stake and otherwise profit from Fifa’s most valuable assets."

‌



View 2 Images Infantino's position has come under scrutiny in recent weeks (Image: Zac Goodwin/PA Wire)

The fallout of the proposals have left the two governing bodies at war, although UEFA has now dropped the threat of its nations boycotting future World Cup tournaments.

UEFA are also pushing for Joshua Kushner, a venture capitalist and the son-in-law of Donald Trump who was set to be the lead investor in FFE, for a testimony.

Article continues below

Kushner apologised for the abandoned venture on Sunday, saying: "While we stand behind the motivations of FFE, we failed to appreciate the political dynamics of global football, and the lengths some would go to… had we known what this would devolve into, we would not have gotten involved."

News.title: Joanna Lumley joins vigil for Nepal flood victims and says catastrophe could have been predicted
News.content:
Joanna Lumley joins vigil for Nepal flood victims and says catastrophe could have been predicted

A candlelit vigil for the devastating flash floods in Nepal was joined by iconic actress Dame Joanna Lumley, who said the disaster 'broke her heart'

View 5 Images Dame Joanna Lumley joins members of London's Nepalese community for a candlelit vigil (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA Wire)

Dame Joanna Lumley joined a vigil for the deadly flash floods in Nepal and said the "heartbreaking" disaster "could have maybe been predicted".

‌



The actress, 80, has visited Nepal on numerous occasions and has strong ties with the community due to her late father being an officer in the Gurkha regiment. Dame Joanna joined members of London's Nepalese community as around 50 people gathered for a candlelit vigil at Panas Gurkha Restaurant in Blackheath, south-east London, on Thursday afternoon.

‌



She said seeing the flash floods sweep through the northern part of the country "broke her heart". Since the floods on August 26, 1,252 people have died and around 4,200 remain missing, including 590 foreign nationals from 34 countries.

‌



Newlywed wife's heartbreaking last words to Brit husband before vanishing in Nepal floods READ MORE :

Forecasters fear 'intense' El Nino effect to last until at least February READ MORE :

View 5 Images The actress said the floods 'broke her heart' (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA Wire)

On Tuesday, Foreign Office minister Lord Wood of Anfield told the House of Lords that 36 British people are currently unaccounted for, up from the previous total of 33.

At the vigil, Dame Joanna said: "I think, actually, in this country and around the world our hearts have been absolutely broken by what happened in Nepal. The sense that it could have maybe been predicted by all the people who understood that by human activities somehow the world seems to be changing, seems to be getting warmer.

‌



View 5 Images Dame Joanna has strong links with Nepal and the Gurkha community (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA Wire)

"These catastrophes, the great Himalayan glaciers melting, isn't something that we haven’t heard of and thought of before. When you see the catastrophic outcome, I think we feel completely hopeless every day we look in the papers." The actress also said having visited Nepal, "it breaks my heart because I know how difficult it is to get around".

Dame Joanna is the patron of healthcare charity Doctors for Nepal and vice patron of The Gurkha Welfare Trust, which provides aid to Gurkha veterans who served in the British Army. Her father served in the 6th Gurkha Rifles, a regiment of the British Indian Army, during the Second World War.

‌



View 5 Images The actress was joined at the vigil with around 50 other people (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA Wire)

The actress emphasised the impact climate change has had on the world. The floods are believed to have been caused by a glacial collapse in the Himalayas which sent rock, ice and meltwater into valleys below, triggering powerful floods.

Dame Joanna said: "It seems that we have been warned about this over the years. Now, there are two camps, as we both know: there is the people who believe that climate change is largely affected by mankind and those who just say that it's completely a natural phenomenon.

Article continues below

View 5 Images Dame Joanna shared her concerns about climate change (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA Wire)

"I belong to the first camp, which is that I do believe that what we do here, and the fossil fuels we burn and the plastic waste in the sea and so on, I do believe that is making the world a sicker place and a weaker place. And the places which are melting fastest are the high mountains and places, and so the Himalayas are there."

Also present at the vigil on Thursday were Vice Lord-Lieutenant Colonel Jane Davis, former Coronation Street star Sally Lindsay, drummer Steve White and Greenwich mayor David Wardrop. Panas Gurkha Restaurant, where the vigil took place, has been raising money to help with the rescue efforts in Nepal.

News.title: Mum slams school for sending teen daughter home over the length of her skirt
News.content:
Mum slams school for sending teen daughter home over the length of her skirt

A row has broken out at a school over the uniform just days after pupils returned - a mum claimed her daughter has been sent home twice and now 'doesn't even want to go to school'

View 2 Images A mum claimed her daughter was sent home twice due to the length of her skirt (Image: ChronicleLive)

A mum has raged after her daughter's school sent her child home twice in a row over the length of her skirt.

‌



The mother, 46, claimed her 15-year-old girl was told to go home at 12.30pm on Wednesday and 9.10am on Thursday as her skirt was 1cm above the knee. This parent, who did not want to be named, claimed her daughter was one of many pupils sent home from Walbottle Academy, in Newcastle, after returning to school from the summer holidays.

‌



The parent, whose daughter is starting Year 11, claimed other pupils were told to go home as their trousers were too tight or too flared.

‌



Parents told sinister danger hiding behind a simple back-to-school photo READ MORE :

UK-wide police reminder as children return to school this week READ MORE :

View 2 Images The uniform row broke out at Walbottle Academy, in Newcastle (Image: Simon Greener/Newcastle Chronicle)

This mother said her daughter did not feel comfortable wearing trousers. She added that she wasn't able to purchase a longer skirt for the pupil and claimed the next size up was too big and did not stay up on her child.

The parent, speaking to the ChronicleLive, said: "You wouldn't believe how many students have been sent home. Everyone is saying it's ridiculous. Twelve of her friends were sent home yesterday.

‌



"Some people haven't even sent their kids into school today. I will just keep sending her in. She's going tomorrow with the same skirt and she's probably going to get sent home tomorrow! My daughter is doing her GCSEs and this is the most important year for her."

The mum said the uniform fallout has impacted her daughter and claimed the 15-year-old has been left not wanting to go to school. The mother added: "She was dead excited to go to school. I woke up at half past six to wake her up and she was already dressed for school.

"This has thrown a spanner in the works. She doesn't even want to go to school. She said 'I really feel self-conscious about wearing trousers. I'm trying to pull it down but it won't go past my hips'. Not every single girl is the same size.

‌



"I don't want her to feel uncomfortable when she goes to school. For her, wearing a skirt is better. We have tried as hard as we can, but I can’t afford to get my daughter's skirt tailored to their specific needs.

"I'm totally frustrated. I just want her to go to school. It's a massive year for her. I feel like it's to the detriment of my daughter's learning."

Walbottle Academy issued a document for parents ahead of the new school year which contained the uniform expectations. It said skirts must be worn at least on the knee in length and they must be worn with tights of at least 60 denier. The school said that trousers must be a tailored trouser material and must not be skinny fit or tight trousers or flared leggings/jeggings.

‌



The mum, who purchased the skirt from Asda, said: "I'm not buying her trousers because she doesn't want them and I can't buy another skirt that will fit her. I think they have got to give a bit of give and take. Fair enough the skirts need to be a certain length as some can wear them a bit short. If it's up their bums I get it but it's not.

"I think they're trying to make a point because they couldn’t introduce the rule of having to wear trousers, which is what they were supposed to do this year. Last year, they wanted to implement trousers and there was a big kick off. I feel really annoyed because I just want her to go to school."

The Northern Education Trust, which runs Walbottle Academy, in a comment to the ChronicleLive said it could not comment on individual cases but encouraged parents "with any concerns to speak directly to the academy".

Article continues below

In a statement, the trust said: "Our uniform expectations were shared with families throughout last academic year and most recently on 26th June, 2nd July, 17th July and 24th August. Assemblies took place with students well in advance of the summer holidays. Information was also shared approximately 15 times over social media throughout the summer holidays.

"All our policies are applied consistently and fairly. To support families and remove barriers, we have invested significantly in brand new uniform which we have given free of charge to families that have come into the academy and worked with us."

The Mirror has reached out to Northern Education Trust and Walbottle Academy for comment.

News.title: UK's biggest gas storage site 'practically empty' - raising threat of even higher bills
News.content:
UK's biggest gas storage site 'practically empty' - raising threat of even higher bills

Wholesale energy prices in Europe have had a new three-year high, just as the UK's most critical has storage site is all-but empty

View 3 Images Rising concerns the UK's gas storage levels come as energy bills are already at a three year high (Image: coldsnowstorm via Getty Images)

The boss of British Gas owner Centrica has revealed a storage site critical for the UK’s winter energy needs is “practically empty” - raising the threat of higher bills.

‌



Chris O’Shea ramped up pressure on the government to back its plans for £2billion of investment in its Rough facility, beneath the North Sea. The former gas field could store enough gas for up to 30 days, but needs to be upgraded.

‌



Sources say Rough has no gas stored in at now, and that Centrica hasn't pumped any into it this year. It only contains so-called “native” gas, or what has always been there, and there is very little of that left too. The facility only has a production licence until next April, meaning it will not be allowed to extract even the native gas after that point.

‌



View 3 Images Centrica's Rough storage site

Writing in The Times, Mr O’Shea said: “Rough, in the North Sea, is the UK’s only large-scale gas storage facility. Yet it is practically empty, as markets currently do not make it financially viable.

‌



"Storage is an insurance policy against supply disruption and price spikes. But if the government chooses not to include Rough in its existing regulatory support model, it will remain empty over the winter and close by spring, losing hundreds of unionised, well-paid jobs.”

His warnings come as European wholesale gas prices hit a three year high, driven by fresh missile strikes in the Middle East. The UK has traditionally had much lower levels of stored gas because it has been able to rely on North Sea supplies.

However, with that source of gas now reducing, and controversy over new North Sea drilling, the country has been forced to call on ever more imports. Yet those routes are under pressure because the Iran war - and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz - has meant Europe’s gas storage levels are also lower than usual ahead of winter.

Article continues below

View 3 Images Centrica boss Chris O'Shea is calling on government guarantees before it commits £2billion for investment in Rough gas storage site (Image: PA Archive/PA Images)

Gas storage sites across the EU were 65% full at the start of this month, down from a five-year average of 82% at the same date. To make matters worse, the Middle East conflict has seen a growing clamour for shipments of liquefied natural gas, especially from Asia.

The rise in wholesale gas prices increases the prospect of further energy bill hikes for households in, who already face an average £60 increase in their annual bill from October after a rise in regulator Ofgem’s price cap to £1,723 a year, a three-year high.

News.title: Donald Trump launches vile racist rant attacking Sadiq Khan and lying about 'no-go areas'
News.content:
Donald Trump launches vile racist rant attacking Sadiq Khan and lying about 'no-go areas'

Trump claimed there are areas of London where police are afraid to go, because a "different culture" had entered, and that Sadiq Khan was only kept in power by the votes of immigrants

View 2 Images Trump launched another vile attack on Sadiq Khan (Image: Yui Mok/PA Wire)

Donald Trump launched a vile, racist rant attacking London Mayor Sadiq Khan and lying about "no go" areas in the UK capital.

‌



Trump trotted out the string of falsehoods in an 'interview' with GB News' Bev Turner. And he said Sir Sadiq was "not somebody that should be representing London and the UK, but he stays there because I guess he has enough votes in the people that are coming in that nobody's going to vote him out". Trump claimed that 20 years ago, "you didn't have crime in London. London was a very safe place, and now you have a different culture that has entered, you know, entered London. Same thing with Paris. I mean, it's a different culture, different people."

‌



He went on: "I mean, if you go through London, London's a much different place. You have a terrible mayor. He's a nasty guy, nasty person. He's a very bad mayor. You have crime that's very high, and London's a very much different place than if you took somebody from 15 or 20 years ago and brought them through London, they wouldn't know what happened. Such a different place."

‌



Ms Turner noted hospitalisations have gone down in the last five years - and that Sir Sadiq was incredibly popular, being re-elected three times. But she went on to claim, without evidence, that some areas of London are a "monoculture".

View 2 Images Trump made a string of false claims about London (Image: Pool/ABACA/Shutterstock)

Trump responded: "You have areas in Paris and London where the police don't want to even go in them, there's no law and order. They're afraid to go in them. E they're afraid or they just don't, you know? They don't want to lose their life. But they run their own, and then you have Sharia courts, and you have lots of other things taking place, and you have a mayor who's absolutely terrible."

‌



There are no Sharia courts in London.

Sharia councils exist, to provide advice on religious matters or offer voluntary adjudication on Muslim marriages - but they have absolutely no power in British law. Similarly, Ecclesiastical Courts in the Church of England and Canon Law Tribunals in the Catholic Church both operate in the UK, offering similar voluntary arbitration on religious and marital matters.

Trump went on: "I mean, he's absolutely a terrible representative for the UK. This is not somebody that should be representing London and the UK, but he stays there because I guess he has enough votes in the people that are coming in that nobody's going to vote him out. You know, democracy." Only British citizens, EU citizens and members of the Commonwealth can vote in London Mayoral elections.

‌



Trump and Sir Sadiq have been at loggerheads since at least 2015, when Sir Sadiq criticised Trump's suggestion that Muslims should be banned from travelling to the US. The London Mayor later branded the US President's view on Islam as "ignorant".

In 2017 Trump sparked a backlash by misrepresenting his comments about the London Bridge terror attack. The same year Sir Sadiq called for a state visit by the US President to be cancelled, and his office gave permission for a giant blimp depicting Trump as an angry baby to be flown in protests.

Following another spat in 2019, the US President wrote on X: "He is a stone cold loser who should focus on crime in London, not me."

Article continues below

Last year Trump launched another attack, describing the London Mayor as "a horrible, vicious, disgusting mayor". In April Sir Sadiq criticised the US commander-in-chief's foul-mouthed threats toward Iran, saying: “I think it's, frankly, gratuitously offensive for the leader of the free world to talk about a civilisation in this way."

News.title: Driver 'runs from scene' of three-car crash as emergency services close road in Bootle
News.content:
Driver 'runs from scene' of three-car crash as emergency services close road in Bootle

Emergency services closed the road after being called out the three-car crash at a busy junction

View Image One driver is reported to have fled the scene of the crash in Bootle (Image: Submitted)

A driver ran from the scene of a three-car pile-up in Bootle on Thursday afternoon as emergency services raced to the scene.

‌



Debris was strewn across the busy junction after the smash, which saw three cars damaged. The road was closed while emergency services helped the remaining drivers and passengers.

‌



Southport Road was closed between Burnie Avenue and Wolfenden Avenue following the crash at around 5.30pm today. Photographs taken at the scene showed one car positioned sideways across the road, badly damaged with its front bumper and bonnet smashed. A second vehicle could be seen parked at the side of the road nearby.

‌



A Merseyside Fire and Rescue spokesman said that the occupants of two of the cars involved in the crash remained at the scene and were unhurt, but the occupants of a third vehicle had fled, Liverpool Echo reports.

He said: "Fire crews were called to a road traffic collision this evening on Southport Road, Bootle. Crews were alerted at 5.27pm and on scene at 5.34pm, with two fire engines in attendance.

Article continues below

"Crews arrived to find three cars involved in a collision at the junction with Kier Hardie Avenue, all vehicles were on all four wheels. "The occupants of one vehicle had left the scene before the arrival of crews, the occupants of the remaining two vehicles were out of the vehicles on arrival and uninjured.

"Crews isolated the battery to one vehicle and applied an absorbent material to the area to make the scene safe. Merseyside Police were in attendance managing traffic. Crews left the scene in the hands of police at 5.55pm."

The road had reopened after emergency services left the scene at 6.40pm.

News.title: Boy, 16, arrested after police chase crash - two officers injured
News.content:
Boy, 16, arrested after police chase crash - two officers injured

Police said they received reports of a car being stolen in Grimsby before a teenager allegedly collided with a marked police vehicle, leaving two officers injured

View Image Two police officers were taken to hospital (stock) (Image: James Maloney/Lancs Live)

A 16-year-old boy has been arrested after allegedly crashing into a marked police car during a chase, leaving two officers injured.

Humberside Police said they received reports of a car being stolen on Byron Grove in Grimsby at around 1pm on Wednesday, September 2. Two police officers were taken to hospital following the collision.

A teenager has since been charged with several offences and remanded in secure accommodation.

"At around 1pm officers received reports of a car being stolen resulting in a pursuit," a Humberside Police spokesperson said.

"The car then allegedly collided with a marked police vehicle, resulting in both vehicles coming to a stop and two officers being taken to hospital to receive treatment to injuries."

The 16-year-old, who cannot be named for legal reasons, has been charged with ten offences, reports Grimsby Live.

This includes dangerous driving, possession of a class C drug, theft, two counts of driving without a licence, two counts of driving without insurance and making off without payment.

The boy is also charged with taking a motor vehicle, possession of a class B drug, aggravated vehicle taking and driving a vehicle without the owner's consent.

Article continues below

He has been remanded into secure accommodation to appear at court at a later date.

News.title: Guinness depot raided as brazen thieves steal 70,000 pints worth £115k
News.content:
Guinness depot raided as brazen thieves steal 70,000 pints worth £115k

Police said the thieves took off with two HGV trailers filled with £115,000 worth of Guinness - equalling 70,000 pints - at an industrial estate in Runcorn, Cheshire

View 2 Images Two HGV trailers carrying more than 800 barrels were spotted at the scene (Image: doram via Getty Images)

More than than 70,000 pints worth of Guinness has been stolen by thieves who took two HGV trailers from a depot, police have said.

‌



The trailers were carrying around 800 barrels of the stout - worth an estimated £115,000 - before they were driven away from an industrial estate in Runcorn on Monday, a Cheshire Constabulary spokesman said.

‌



Officers are now appealing for witnesses who may have seen a lorry entering the Aston Lane area at about 7.45pm, to contact them.

‌



The vehicle is said to have connected to an HGV trailer containing the Guinness before leaving the site at around 7.55pm and driving towards the Mersey Gateway bridge.

A second lorry arrived at 9.12pm and connected to another trailer, which also contained barrels of Guinness. That lorry left at 9.30pm and headed in the direction of Rainhill and Watkinson Way.

View 2 Images The trailers were carrying around 800 barrels of Guinness (Image: Cheshire Constabulary/PA Wire)

‌



The stolen HGVs are believed to have been driven away by men, police said. The first driver is described as white with a short dark beard and he was wearing a beanie hat, while the second is believed to have been wearing a cap.

Detectives say the barrels, containing around 70,400 pints of the Irish tipple, had been intended to be delivered to pubs.

Diageo, which owns Guinness, has a packaging warehouse on the Whitehouse Industrial Estate on Aston Lane. It is estimated the total value of the items stolen - the Guinness and the trailers themselves - is around £205,000.

Article continues below

The missing trailers are described as white tri-axle curtain side trailers with branding for logistics company GXO on their curtains and rear doors.

The trucks have the unique ID numbers DL736 and DL542 on the top left corner of their rear doors.

Cheshire Constabulary has appealed for anyone with information, or any drivers who may have dashcam footage, to contact them on the website, or by calling 101 and using incident reference number IML-2408641.

News.title: Farage senior aide filmed suggesting way to avoid donations law
News.content:
Nigel Farage's senior aide suggested a way to get around electoral law to secure a foreign donation of Â£500,000 for Reform UK, according to undercover filming broadcast by Channel 4.

Dan Jukes was filmed meeting a man posing as the British-based son of a rich American businessman.

Electoral law sets out that to be a permissible donor to a UK political party you must be a UK registered voter, or a company registered in the UK.

In this instance, the son would be a permissible donor, his father would not be.

The undercover filming was done by a group called Verbatim Investigations, which was founded by journalists from the Centre for Climate Reporting. Channel 4 News say they have verified the material they were given and chose to broadcast.

Reform UK denies any wrongdoing and claims to have "been the target of a hoax perpetuated by foreign funded climate change activists".

The reporter posing as the son of the American donor is filmed raising a concern that his father wouldn't be able to directly donate to the party within the law.

Filmed standing outside a pub in Westminster, Jukes said "you do realise that you can do it?"

Channel 4 say Jukes was suggesting that the donation could be in the UK-based son's name, although the money would have come from his American father.

"Actually that does strike me as a solution," Jukes continues.

He then claims they have done it several times before, in exchanges bleeped out but which appear to refer to other instances where this mechanism had been used before.

"That's one of the ways in which we do it," he is recorded as saying.

Reform UK have launched an internal investigation into Jukes. They would not confirm if he remained a party spokesperson.

Later, Channel 4 broadcast footage from a lunch in Clacton in Essex, with both the reporter posing as the UK-based son, and an actor â his supposed American father. Opposite them are both Dan Jukes and the Reform UK leader Nigel Farage.

Farage says "it's all above board" after the son has told him he has been in discussions with both Jukes and Reform's Head of Policy, James Orr about it for some time.

"I'll be the registered donor," the son says. "But then dad will send the money to me, and then as soon as that's done and all those conversations are had the money is available."

"Thank you. Well, both of you. Thank you," Farage is heard saying.

Orr is also now the subject of an internal Reform UK investigation.

News.title: Schools to close early for A66 crash funeral amid safety concerns
News.content:
Supt John Wrintmore from Cleveland Police said there was potential for traffic disruption and delays from 15:00 to 17:00 on Friday.

"This will affect areas of South Bank, Normanby Road through Teesville, Ormesby and Marton, and Acklam Road," he said.

"We are working closely with highways departments from the local authority, who are leading on the traffic management for this event, in order to minimise disruption.

"As with any significant gathering, we have plans in place to ensure public safety and security, which is line with our usual process."

A spokesperson for Redcar & Cleveland Borough Council said: "A number of schools in the South Bank area will close earlier than usual on Friday afternoon due to anticipated traffic congestion and transport disruption associated with a local funeral taking place in the area.

"The decision was made after careful consideration of the potential impact on home-to-school transport and the departure of pupils, staff and families at the end of the school day.

"Schools have worked with the Local Authority and transport providers to consider arrangements for pupils, including those who travel to and from specialist educational settings.

"We recognise that early closure may cause inconvenience for some parents and carers, and we thank them for their understanding and cooperation."

The decision comes after a vigil, for one of the young men who died, last week was followed by disorder in Haswell, County Durham, where a number of cars were set on fire.

The incident prompted criticism from MPs and police.

The Volkswagen Passat involved in the collision was being pursued by police until 10 seconds before the crash, according to the police watchdog.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct said the Passat was believed to be using cloned registration plates.

A total of 27 people have been arrested as part of a wider police operation against organised crime, following the crash.
