Sports.title: Will Enzo Fernandez start for Man City immediately after £125m Chelsea transfer?
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez is the joint most expensive player in British football history after his mega-money move from Chelsea to Manchester City.

And the £125m midfielder will be itching to make his debut for his new club.



2 Fernandez has been reunited with his old Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca at Man City Credit: AFP

Man City, who have won their first two Premier League games under Enzo Maresca, are back in action at home to Coventry on Saturday.

Will Fernandez start for Man City against Coventry?

Following the summer arrivals of Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi – also for substantial fees – City certainly have no shortage of quality options in midfield.

Anderson started the wins over Bournemouth and Crystal Palace, with Bouaddi replacing him from the bench for his debut late on in the latter game.



And while 18-year-old Bouaddi is undoubtedly one of the most prodigious midfield talents around, Maresca may feel a need to ease him into the rigours of the Premier League.

Fernandez, by contrast, has been there and done it, spending the last three-and-a-half years with Chelsea.



He's also got some minutes in the tank already this term, making what proved to be his final appearance for the Blues as a substitute in their opening-weekend win at Fulham.

As such, one would expect him to be in contention to start for City this weekend.



That could be bad news for Nico O'Reilly, who started in a more advanced midfield role against Bournemouth before playing deeper against Palace.

And with Josko Gvardiol starting the campaign so well in the England international's slightly more natural left-back role, scoring the winner against Bournemouth and providing an assist last time out, O'Reilly may have to make do with a spot on the bench for the visit of Coventry.

Will City's other new signings play?

City have made two other signings since their last outing, both wingers.

2 City won the race to sign Ndiaye Credit: Getty



Brazilian Allan joined from Palmeiras on the penultimate day of the transfer window, with Iliman Ndiaye arriving from Everton on deadline day.

But neither is likely to dislodge Phil Foden or Antoine Semenyo – both of whom set up goals in the 4-1 victory over Palace – so will probably find themselves among the substitutes in the first instance.

What has Enzo Fernandez said?

Speaking after completing his switch to City, Fernandez expressed his desire to go to another level. He said: "I could not be happier to be here, and I am ready for the challenge of helping City continue winning trophies. This is a club built for success.

"If you look across the squad, City have quality in every area. I want to learn from my new teammates and become a better player.



"I pride myself on continually improving my game. Anyone who’s worked with me will know how hard I train every single day and how much I put into matches. I give absolutely everything and I can promise Manchester City that will continue now I’m here."

What have City fans said?

The signing of Fernandez has divided opinion among City fans following his antics for Argentina at the World Cup.

But one supporter who's certainly excited to have him onboard is Noel Gallagher, who told talkSPORT he admired Fernandez's 'ballsy' nature.

Sports.title: Viktor Gyokeres told he is ‘lucky’ to be at Arsenal just one year after £64m transfer
Sports.content:
Viktor Gyokeres told he is ‘lucky’ to be at Arsenal just one year after £64m transfer

Troy Deeney believes Viktor Gyokeres considers himself fortunate to remain an Arsenal player now the transfer window has closed.

The striker was linked with a summer exit just a year after becoming a Gunner with his £63.7million move from Sporting.

2 Gyokeres has not played a single minute in the league this season Credit: Getty

Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez became a dream target for the Premier League champions amid fellow interest from Barcelona.

talkSPORT reported that, to supplement a potential deal, Arsenal explored the possibility of offering Gyokeres during their initial talks.

Alvarez did not sign for the Gunners and, therefore, Gyokeres did not leave, with Mikel Arteta insisting that he would remain at the club.

However, the Sweden international has not featured in either of their Premier League victories against Coventry City and Aston Villa.

Kai Havertz has been the preferred option up top so, with Gyokeres struggling for minutes, Deeney senses he has had some fortune.

"I think he knows he's lucky to be there, personally," he said on the Premier League All Access podcast for talkSPORT.

"I think when you look at his career, look at his attributes, he's probably going, 'I'm at a team here, I've won the Premier League, this is unbelievable'.

"He will be used in the Champions League, but also there's a business element to this where sometimes, things just get swept under the rug now.

"He'll have a conversation, I wouldn't be surprised if we start seeing over the next two, three weeks, he gets more minutes and more time now the window's closed.

"Mikel is not stupid enough to just keep him on the outside, he'll be like, 'Alright, you're still here, you're part of the squad, let's move forward.'"

2 Havertz sits top of the pecking order at Arsenal Credit: Getty

Could Gyokeres play for Arsenal against Chelsea?

After being an unused substitute in the wins over Coventry and Villa, Gyokeres is waiting for his first league appearance.

Havertz was quiet at Villa Park as he managed just one shot, but he is likely to return to the starting XI this weekend.

Arsenal host Chelsea in the headline Premier League clash on Sunday, with both sides having a 100 per cent record thus far.

Gyokeres looks set to be named on the bench for a third consecutive match, but could earn his first outing.

Now that Gabriel Jesus has left for Barcelona, the 28-year-old joins Havertz as the only striker options at Arsenal.

Sports.title: Jadon Sancho handed Jesse Lingard warning amid ‘fascinating’ free transfer links
Sports.content:
Jadon's Sancho's rumoured move to Brazilian club Palmeiras would be 'fascinating' were it to come to fruition.

That's the view of South American football expert Tim Vickery, with Sancho linked with a surprise switch to the three-time Copa Libertadores winners.



2 Sancho's last appearance for Manchester United came in the 2024 Community Shield Credit: Getty

The winger is a free agent after leaving Manchester United at the end of his contract this summer.

And should he head to Brazil, he'll follow in the footsteps of former United teammate Jesse Lingard, who joined Corinthians back in March.

Vickery keen on Sancho to Palmeiras

However, Vickery stressed that it wouldn't be the same kind of move – with Lingard now 33 and Sancho, at 26, still theoretically in his prime.



He told talkSPORT's Hawksbee and Jacobs: "They've [Palmeiras] got a week to sort this one out [the Brazilian transfer window closes next Friday, September 11].

"Jesse Lingard is over here with Corinthians. He's not done very much; he's not getting a game. But obviously Jadon Sancho is at a very different stage in his career.



"They've just sold Allan to Man City, picked up one or two injuries…it would be fascinating, it really would. I'm hoping it happens.

"They're in three competitions. Top of the Brazilian league, quarter-finals of the Libertadores, semi-finals of the Brazilian Cup.



"There's loads and loads to play for, so he can keep himself in the international shop window coming over on a short-term deal.

"Bring it on – I'd love to see it happen."

Sancho's United nightmare

Sancho joined Man United from Borussia Dortmund for £73m in 2021 but failed to live up to his price tag.

2 Sancho signed for Man United when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer was manager Credit: Getty

After two unconvincing seasons with Old Trafford, during which he dropped out of the England squad, he was loaned back to Dortmund in 2023.



Further loan spells with Chelsea and Aston Villa followed, but Sancho looked a shadow of the player he was during his breakthrough years in the Bundesliga.

A move to Brazil would be a left-field one, but it could be just what he needs to kickstart his career – away from the glaring limelight of the European game.

Trailblazing Lingard

Lingard became the first Englishman to play in the Brazilian top flight when he arrived after leaving South Korea's FC Seoul at the end of last year.

He is, however, one of a number of European players currently plying their trade in the Brasileirao.



They include another of Lingard's former United colleagues, Netherlands striker Memphis Depay, who has been at Corinthians since 2024, and ex-Chelsea and Spain midfielder Saul of Flamengo.

Sports.title: Estevao ‘impatient’ as Chelsea’s £160m best friend duo send Brazilian star down pecking order
Sports.content:
Estevao ‘impatient’ as Chelsea’s £160m best friend duo send Brazilian star down pecking order

Estevao Willian could be growing impatient at Chelsea following the signing of fellow attacker Morgan Rogers.

That's according to Tim Vickery, with the Brazilian starlet facing new competition in his second season at Stamford Bridge.

3 It's not been an easy start for Estevao at Chelsea this season Credit: Getty

After officially arriving from Palmeiras last summer, Estevao delivered a hugely impressive debut campaign in English football at Chelsea.

He played 36 times, scored eight goals and assisted four others as he turned into one of the most exciting Premier League prospects.

A hamstring injury ended his season early and he missed out on the World Cup with Brazil having looked set to be named in their squad.

Over the summer, Chelsea made the club-record £117million signing of Rogers, who is best friends with his England co-star Cole Palmer.

The duo started in their league wins over Fulham and Brighton, as well as the Carabao Cup victory against Luton Town.

Estevao on the other hand has earned just one start and, although it is still early in the season, the 19-year-old may just be slightly restless.

Has Estevao become 'impatient' at Chelsea?

Speaking to talkSPORT, South American football journalist Vickery addressed the potential unhappiness and said: "He chose Chelsea.

"It's the first real, genuine, Brazilian superstar to choose Chelsea over the likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona.

"Maybe he just feels that he's fallen a little bit down the pecking order with Morgan Rogers, who is Cole Palmer's great mate, coming in.

"So, maybe there's a little bit of impatience there, we will find out.

3 Palmer and Rogers have become a go-to attacking pair at Chelsea Credit: Getty

"It is a shame because he gave us some fantastic (performances)... the injury is unfortunate, because I wonder what he might have done at the World Cup because (Carlo) Ancelotti loves him.

"Running into that injury was a little bit unfortunate, but it's doubly unfortunate for me if Chelsea can't give him a regular gig because I think he's just a fantastic talent."

Rogers and Palmer success this season

With both players academy graduates at Manchester City, Rogers and Palmer reunited at club level when the former signed for Chelsea.

They made an excellent start to the season in the 3-2 win at Fulham as each player found the target, whilst Palmer also bagged an assist.

Rogers provided for Pedro Neto in the 4-3 triumph against Brighton, whilst his long-term friend scored a second.

It was a quiet night at the office for the pair when they hosted Luton.

3 Estevao will hope for more regular minutes as the season progresses Credit: Getty

Instead, it was Estevao who impressed for Xabi Alonso's side as his shot went off Hakeem Odoffin for an own-goal during the 2-0 win.

Alonso is likely to stick with Rogers and Palmer playing alongside the in-form Joao Pedro when they visit Arsenal on Sunday.

Sports.title: Chelsea announce signing of Brazilian prodigy 48 hours after transfer window shuts
Sports.content:
Chelsea have confirmed the signing of 18-year-old Brazilian full-back Denner from Corinthians.

Denner, who starred for Corinthians' Under-20 side, has signed an eight-year deal with the Blues.

2 Denner will link up with Chelsea's age-group squads at their Cobham training base Credit: Getty

The teenager will link up with Cobham Next Gen (CNG), Chelsea's newly rebranded Under-19 and Under-21 squads.

Denner's rapid rise

Denner joined the youth set-up of hometown club Corinthians at the age of 13.

By 16, he was representing them at U-20 level, helping that team finish as runners-up in the Sao Paulo Youth Cup.

He scored the opening goal in the final as Corinthians were beaten by Sao Paulo.

Chelsea reportedly first agreed a deal for Denner back in 2025 with a view to signing him this year.

He's one of three academy signings the Blues have made this summer, following midfielder Harrison Bettoni from Wigan and defender Alfie Osborne from Hearts.

An attack-minded full-back whose naturally position is on the left, Denner has played for Brazil up to Under-17 level.

He was part of the squad that won the 2025 South American Under-17 Championship.

According to Brazilian media, Denner is a cousin of Arsenal star Gabriel.

And if he follows anything like the career trajectory of the Premier League title-winning Gunners centre-back, Chelsea have a very special talent indeed on their hands.

2 Gabriel may come up against a family member in the next few years Credit: Getty

Chelsea's lucrative window

This summer's transfer window was another hugely busy one for Chelsea.

As well as spending over £300m to bring in players such as Moran Rogers and Maxence Lacroix, the Blues made around £400m in player sales.

A substantial chunk of their total income came from the sale of Enzo Fernandez alone.

The midfielder joined Manchester City on deadline day for £125m.

That fee equalled the record in British football paid by Liverpool to sign Alexander Isak from Newcastle last year.

Tosin Adarabioyo and Marc Guiu also made deadline-day moves away from Stamford Bridge, heading to Tottenham and RB Leipzig respectively.

Sports.title: ‘Toothless’ Premier League side warned of relegation threat after ‘uninspiring’ transfer window
Sports.content:
Fulham are heading towards Premier League relegation and showed a lack of motivation in the summer transfer window.

That's the view of talkSPORT host Max Scott as the west London side bemoan a worrying start to the season with two defeats in two.

4 Fulham could be battling for Premier League survival this season Credit: Getty

After a 3-2 home loss to local rivals Chelsea, Sunderland beat Fulham 1-0 on Sunday to ensure they remain without a point in the league.

With Liverpool and Manchester United two of their upcoming tests, new boss Alvaro Arbeloa faces an uphill climb at Craven Cottage.

But, even with 36 more games to play this season, Scott can only see one outcome for the Cottagers - relegation to the Championship.

Speaking on NO BS for talkSPORT, he explained why he tipped Fulham to finish in the bottom three of the Premier League amid their poor start.

"We're going to talk about Sunderland v Fulham," Scott said.

"For me, it was a relegation six-pointer. I have backed Hull, Sunderland and Fulham to go down.

"I'm questioning Hull, I'm not so sure about Sunderland, I still think they're going to be down there. Fulham? They're absolute goners."

Co-host Olly Clink labelled the Cottagers 'terrible' as Scott continued: "Limp-wristed, and no wonder Arbeloa has already lost his rag in his post-match comments after the game.

"I just think... I know this sounds harsh, but what are Fulham?"

Do Fulham regret losing Marco Silva?

Scott once again tipped Fulham for the drop, and then questioned why the club didn't do enough to keep former manager Silva.

4 Arbeloa is winless in the Premier League Credit: Getty

4 Fulham may be left to rue letting Silva leave Credit: Getty

The Portuguese left at the end of last season amid the expiration of his contract in June and is now at Benfica, where has won six of his nine games in charge.

Arbeloa replaced him following a spell at Real Madrid, but it's his predecessor who Scott believes that Fulham should have backed.

Max Scott labels Fulham a 'waste of space'

"Just toothless," Scott said.

"I think, what are they doing not throwing the money at Marco Silva? They have a lot of money in the bank, their owner (Shahid Khan) does. Their stadium, the amount of money they charge Fulham fans...

"They're a waste of space. Give it to Birmingham, give it to Wrexham, that spot, give it to a big club like Sheffield Wednesday in a couple of years if they can get there.

"I just think Fulham are a bit boring. I would never tune into a Fulham game, because Fulham are playing. I would tune into watch Forest play them... I'm just a bit bored of them.

Fulham signings in summer 2026 Gonzalo Garcia - £34m, Real Madrid Shea Charles - £30m, Southampton David Affengruber - £8.6m, Elche Cesar Palacios - £8m, Real Madrid Jonah Kusi-Asare - £5m, Bayern Munich Manuel Angel - £3m, Real Madrid Hugo Larsson - Loan, Eintracht Frankfurt

4 Arbeloa has Fulham sitting 16th in the table Credit: Getty

"And their window has been so uninspiring as well."

"It's a lovely ground," he added. "I've heard from a few players that they really like playing at Fulham, because you don't get the pressure.

"But sometimes, pressure creates diamonds, and there's no diamonds at Fulham at the minute.

"I think they miss the edge that Marco Silva brings, I think they failed to support him adequately in the window, and no wonder he's gone to Benfica.

"If he had been supported, they should have been playing European football and that would have then elevated the club in terms of revenue, players, being an attractive proposition.

"Now, I think they're just going to pale into insignificance in the Premier League and get relegated."

Sports.title: Amanda Staveley locked out of West Ham ownership as Daniel Kretinsky becomes majority shareholder
Sports.content:
Amanda Staveley locked out of West Ham ownership as Daniel Kretinsky becomes majority shareholder

Daniel Kretinsky has agreed a deal with the Gold family to become West Ham's majority shareholder, talkSPORT understands.

As such, Amanda Staveley, who helped lead the Saudi-backed 2024 takeover of Newcastle, has effectively been blocked from buying a stake in the Hammers.

2 Kretinsky is now the Hammers' majority shareholder Credit: Getty

talkSPORT also understands David Sullivan has increased his ownership of the club to 40 per cent.

Following the death of co-chairman David Gold in 2023, his daughter Vanessa took control of a 25.1 per cent share in the club.

Kretinsky's fresh investment

Czech businessman Kretinsky first invested in West Ham back in 2021.

His stake is now set to increase beyond Sullivan's 40 per cent share.

talkSPORT reported last month that Kretinsky had reduced his stake from 27 per cent to below 25 per cent in an effort to prevent Staveley from investing.

The billionaire is believed to have sold part of his share to fellow Czech Jakub Havrlant.

A consortium led by Staveley had been eyeing up the Gold family's stake, worth around £150m.

Sullivan was forced to step down as West Ham chairman in June after accusations of sexual abuse were made against him.

The 77-year-old, who made much of his fortune in the adult entertainment industry, has vehemently denied the claims.

West Ham get their season up and running

This latest development in the Hammers' ownership saga comes amid the beginning of their mission to make an immediate return to the Premier League following relegation last season.

Nuno Espirito Santo's side picked up their first win of the Championship campaign on Tuesday, beating Wolves 4-2 at the London Stadium.

2 Nuno's West Ham got their first league victory of 2026/27 at the fourth time of asking Credit: Getty

Divine Mukasa bagged a brace for the hosts, with Jarrod Bowen and Konstantinos Mavropanos also on the scoresheet.

The result, which came after fans had chanted at their previous game for Nuno to be sacked, took West Ham into the top half of table, a point off the play-offs at this early stage of the season.

Next up for the Hammers is another home game against Derby on Saturday.

West Ham dropped back into the second tier after 14 years in the Premier League, their longest top-flight stint since the 1970s.

Their last Championship stint lasted just one season as they were promoted via the play-offs in 2011/12.

Sports.title: How to watch Cristiano Ronaldo’s next match as Ange Postecoglou bids to continue perfect start
Sports.content:
How to watch Cristiano Ronaldo’s next match as Ange Postecoglou bids to continue perfect start

Cristiano Ronaldo's Al-Nassr will be aiming to make it five Saudi Pro League wins from five under Ange Postecoglou on Saturday.

Al-Nassr have made the perfect start to their title defence and sit second behind league leaders Al-Hilal only on goal difference.

2 Postecoglou boasts a 100% record in charge of Al-Nassr so far Credit: Getty

Former Tottenham boss Postecoglou succeeded Jorge Jesus as head coach this summer and has overseen five wins in all competitions, with Al-Nassr also beating Al-Diriyah in the King's Cup.

And his side are back in action away to Al-Ittihad this Saturday (September 5) at 7pm BST.

How can I watch Ronaldo's next match?

You can stream Al-Ittihad vs Al-Nassr live on talkSPORT.com.

For a small fee, you'll be able to stream every available Saudi Pro League game.

Ronaldo's season so far and what's next

Ronaldo scored his second goal of the campaign as Al-Nassr came from behind to beat Al-Taawoun 2-1 last time out.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner has made three Saudi Pro League appearances so far this term as he continues to captain the club – though he didn't take kindly to being substituted in the recent 3-2 win over Al-Ettifaq.

However, he has admitted the 2026/27 season is likely to be his last.

The 41-year-old, who has one year left on his contract at the Riyadh-based club, told Vogue last month an interview about his wedding to Georgina Rodriguez: "This is probably my last year of football, and I want to leave a spectacular legacy.

"I have my future all mapped out. I have so many things to keep me busy that to tell you just one thing is hard. Because football could leave a big hole, you have to fill your time in various ways, not just one.

"Have more fun, travel more, watch and play padel, which I really like, and continue to enjoy what I've earned – what we've earned.

2 Ronaldo has scored well over 100 goals for Al-Nassr Credit: Getty

"Because after all it's been 25 years with a lot of sacrifice."

Ronaldo joined Al-Nassr in 2023 following the end of his second spell with Manchester United.

He's racked up 131 goals in 151 appearances in all competitions so far, averaging almost a goal a game in the Saudi Pro League.

He won the division's Golden Boot in 2023/24 and 2024/25.

Who else can I watch in action for Al-Nassr?

Ronaldo is among a number of former Premier League stars currently plying their trade for Al-Nassr.

He's joined by fellow Portugal international and ex-Chelsea man Joao Felix, as well as Premier League-winning Liverpool great Sadio Mane.

Sports.title: Aston Villa handed major boost as new £60m star Johan Manzambi returns to training - but he may not be risked for Hull clash
Sports.content:
Johan Manzambi trained with his Aston Villa team-mates on Thursday fuelling hopes that his debut could arrive sooner than expected.

The club-record signing from Freiburg had a knee injury when he joined Villa in July in a deal worth up to £60million, and he has yet to play as he continues his recovery.

Yet Daily Mail Sport understands Manzambi took part in Thursday's session, though it is unclear at this stage whether he would be considered for Saturday's trip to Hull, where Villa will hope to claim their first points of the season after consecutive defeats to Brighton and Arsenal.

After the 1-0 home defeat by Arsenal on August 31, Emery was cautious about Manzambi, though he hoped the 20-year-old would be able to join in this week.

He said: 'We must be careful. He had an injury and we want his comeback to be clear and strong, with no risk.

'Progressively, he is working individually and is starting collectively with the group this week.'

Johan Manzambi trained with his Aston Villa team-mates on Thursday as he stepped up his recovery

After losing key members of the team who lifted the Europa League and qualified for the Champions League last term, Villa have tried to rebuild by making 11 signings. Emery has also brought forward Brian Madjo and midfielder George Hemmings into the first-team group.

Morgan Rogers moved to Chelsea this summer for a record £117m, with Emi Martinez also making the switch to Stamford Bridge. Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne, Ollie Watkins and Ezri Konsa also departed in a summer of huge change at Villa Park.

Sports.title: Roy Keane goes viral after leaving Gary Neville and Co in stitches with hilarious comparison between football stat and 'speaking to girls in a nightclub'
Sports.content:
Roy Keane left his Stick to Football colleagues in fits of laughter following his thoughts about the statistic 'Expected Goals' (xG). Speaking on the latest episode of the show, brought to you by Disney+, the former Manchester United captain expressed why he believes that particular stat - which measures the probability that a given shot will result in a goal - is irrelevant. Sitting alongside Gary Neville, Jamie Carragher, Jill Scott and Ian Wright, Keane started his point animatedly with: 'Do you know what that stat is? 'Years ago, when you'd go to a nightclub back in the day, and you'd chat to a girl all night, but you go home by yourself. What's your xG?' Keane's quip left Neville, Carragher, Scott and Wright in stitches. Neville then replied self-depreciatingly: 'Roy, I kept clean sheets!' A smirking Roy said: 'I'm sure you did, yeah!' xG explained the Roy Keane way! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/qJOS705noc — The Overlap (@WeAreTheOverlap) September 3, 2026 Roy Keane left his Stick to Football colleagues laughing with his views on Expected Goals (xG) Gary Neville (left) and Jamie Carragher were in hysterics after Keane compared it to nightclubs During the show, the quintet discussed the closing of the summer transfer window - following Tuesday's 11pm deadline. Among the clubs discussed was Liverpool - with Carragher believing Reds boss Andoni Iraola needs to have an awkward conversation with his vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai and move him to right back permanently. Szoboszlai, 25, was rewarded with a new £350,000-a-week contract this summer after being named Liverpool’s Player of the Season for his impressive performances in midfield last campaign - one of the few positives in what was otherwise a disappointing season for the Reds under Arne Slot. Despite establishing himself as a mainstay in midfield, the Hungarian has also been called upon to deputise at right-back, doing so sporadically last season and again during the second half of Liverpool’s 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest on Saturday. Carragher believes Szoboszlai may be tasked with the right-back role permanently after Liverpool's disjointed start under Iraola, who has drawn both his Premier League matches so far. With Conor Bradley still injured and Jeremie Frimpong struggling for form, right-back has become a problem position for Liverpool since Trent Alexander-Arnold's exit to Real Madrid last summer. Fearing it was a 'massive mistake' not to bolster Liverpool's ranks at full back in the transfer window, Carragher is confident Szoboszlai could provide a solution for Iraola. Carragher believes Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola (right) needs to have an awkward conversation with his vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai (left) and move him to right-back 'The big thing he (Iraola) has got, and it happened last season and at the weekend, Szoboszlai went back to right-back. I've never believed Szoboszlai is a central midfield player,' Carragher said. 'Now, he's signed a new contract and I can only imagine in those talks, they were desperate for him to stay, he's almost said "I want to play midfield". He's moved around a bit and he started the season in central midfield. I don't see him as that. 'For me, in midfield he's a Jordan Henderson. Runner, energy, with more of a goal threat. But Liverpool don't play that way and he's not really a No 10. His best role could actually be at right-back. He'd get plenty of the ball, he can run and almost play that Trent role from there. 'But there's no way he's going to want to play there because he's just signed a new contract for £350,000 a week. You've just done this big thing, he's the vice-captain, I just think that's a conversation Iraola is going to have to have going forward, because the midfield is not right and he's part of that midfield not being right.'

Sports.title: How influencers are killing the US Open and turning it into a 'zoo': Angry top stars hit out at 'disrespectful' and noisy content creators disrupting matches for pictures
Sports.content:
How influencers are killing the US Open and turning it into a 'zoo': Angry top stars hit out at 'disrespectful' and noisy content creators disrupting matches for pictures

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Naomi Osaka was not having the easiest time on court. Having battled through a tie-break to edge the first set, she was serving at 4-4 in the second. Then, her concentration snapped.

Up in the luxury suites, a group of influencers were posing for photographs using a bright, portable light. As they milled about the box, unaware of the tension below, their distraction was enough to prompt a warning from the chair umpire. But it took a few moments for the message to filter through. After all, their focus was on getting the perfect shot.

Welcome to the 2026 US Open. Long the envy of the Grand Slams for the late-night energy and glamour that only New York can provide, this year's tournament has been subject to complaints about being overrun with influencers who see the final major of the year as little more than a creative backdrop on social media.

'People are down there trying to perform, and it's their career and their job. It seems like a bit disrespectful,' US No 1 Jessica Pegula said when asked about the incident in Osaka's match after her own bow on Arthur Ashe, the tournament's biggest court. 'I think it's gotten a little too much, it feels, this year.'

There's no mystery behind why the US Open has become such a popular destination to tick off for the well-travelled influencer.

'The US Open has evolved from a tennis tournament into one of the most powerful cultural points on the New York calendar,' notes Reece Milner, Senior Strategy Manager at The Goat Agency, a creator and influencer marketing shop. 'It now sits at the intersection of sport, fashion, luxury, hospitality, celebrity, lifestyle and content culture.'

The 'rituals' that appear so frequently on social media feeds that you might be able to play US Open bingo, like enjoying a night match, a Honey Deuce cocktail or $100 COQODAQ chicken nugget-and-caviar box, Milner adds, have only served to crystallise its status.

A group of influencers caught flack for using a portable light to take pictures during Naomi Osaka's match

The US Open has seen a huge rise in popularity in recent years and brands hosting influencers at the tournament in a bid to borrow its cultural clout has risen too

This is no one-way street either, with the US Open well aware of its cultural power outside of tennis as well as within. The tournament has embraced the influencer, this year going as far as to credential 100 content creators, with US Open head of communications Brendan McIntyre noting that in years to come, the number is only going to 'go upwards'.

But those influencers aren't necessarily the problem. Tennis media has evolved to take in TikTok, Instagram, and Substack experts, all invested in growing interest in the game itself. More worthy of skepticism are those who might be spending one night at the Open, making it a race against time to get the perfect picture, action on court be damned.

The US Open has never been Wimbledon, and that's a good thing. The noise of an Arthur Ashe night session makes for pleasing whiplash after the prim-and-proper hush of Centre Court as the tour bounces between the two majors.

But as greater numbers of guests flood into the Billie Jean King National Tennis Center with limited interest in the tennis and more on their feed, the noise levels of ambient chatter, rather than engagement in the match, have caused problems for players.

'On Ashe, you hear everything,' Pegula added. 'Even when there's dead noise, there's still a buzz or a chatter or people talking and eating and laughing and all these different kind of emotions. You really have to do a good job of locking yourself in a bubble when you're out there.'

Of fans on the outdoor courts, French player Adrian Mannarino was more forthright: 'They come in any which way, they move around, they talk. It's the tournament that tolerates this, and I don't know if it's the best idea for the game in general. There's noise coming from everywhere. It's become a bit of a zoo.'

Watching Aryna Sabalenka and Carlos Alcaraz on Arthur Ashe on Wednesday, the noise of the crowd never dipped below 'pub garden'. Since the tournament ushered in 'free fan movement' in 2024 which allows fans to come and go without waiting for changeovers or set breaks, the policy has been followed to the letter, with the lower bowl constantly in motion.

Influencers have added to the heat around the US Open and their enviable photographs will have translated, in part, to ticket sales

Inside Arthur Ashe Stadium is a constant hum of noise as fans move in their seats during points

That's where most of the chatter comes from too, with the seats in the gods crammed with fans locked in on the action, and quieter during play.

As Alcaraz took the first game after losing his opening set to Jaime Faria, the noise rises to a roar, with the same staticky thickness of a sound machine playing a recording of the ocean at full volume. At 0-15, clearly distracted, the Portuguese player serves a double fault. The chair umpire gives a warning when a fan shouts down from the stands as he's preparing to serve again, but does little to dim the constant conversation.

Nor have those in the suites learned their lesson. Despite the US Open displaying messages around the site telling fans to refrain from using flash or lights to take pictures, Daily Mail Sport spotted flashes going off during Sabalenka's thrashing of Polina Iatcenko. A statement shared after the Osaka incident placed the responsibility for wrangling misbehaving influencers on the chair umpires, who 'have the ability to address the crowd' when 'infrequent' disruptions occur.

Influencers have added to the heat around the US Open and their enviable photographs will have translated, in part, to ticket sales. But if the goal is to get more fans into the sport, week-in, week-out, they need great tennis played in a great tennis atmosphere - and inside on the tournament's biggest courts, that can no longer be guaranteed.

Sports.title: Revealed: The eight Springbok and All Black superstars being offered to PREM Rugby clubs in blockbuster deals, four England centres on rivals' radars, Chessum's Leicester future and Northampton's plan for Mitchell and McParland
Sports.content:
Beauden Barrett, Malcolm Marx, Ox Nche and Richie Mo'unga are among the global superstars being touted around English clubs for blockbuster signings after next year's World Cup.

Players are already preparing for the next four-year cycle, when Test teams often turn to the next generation. Japan and France have proved the most lucrative destinations in recent seasons but agents are now testing the English market, following investment in the likes of Newcastle, Bath and Exeter.

Barrett, 35, is one of the most decorated players of all time and is likely to surpass Sam Whitelock's All Black record of 153 caps next year, with a current total of 144.

Barrett has played for the Auckland-based Blues since 2020, with brief spells in Japan, and McKenzie is the all-time top points-scorer and try-scorer for the Chiefs.

Nche, 31, and reigning World Rugby Player of the Year Marx, 32, are part of the fearsome Springbok front row that has dominated the sport for the last seven years. Nche plays for the Durban-based Sharks in his homeland while Marx is in Japan with the Kubota Spears.

‘PREM Rugby is in a good place now with the investment so I see a future where, like before, we can bring world-class players into the competition,’ admitted Bristol coach Pat Lam. ‘We already have some of the best players in the world in our competition and now there’s talk about having a second marquee player and the salary cap coming up.’

According to Daily Mail Sport sources, New Zealand have the most players with expiring contracts after next year’s World Cup in Australia. The likes of Will Jordan, Codie Taylor, Scott Barrett and Ardie Savea – who can boast a combined 360 All Blacks caps between them – are also being pitched as players look to secure their futures early.

Will Jordan (left) and Beauden Barrett (right) are being offered to English clubs for potential blockbuster signings after next year's World Cup

Legendary All Black forwards Codie Taylor and Ardie Savea are also being touted

Reigning World Rugby Player of the Year Malcolm Marx, 32, is also being offered around

Four England stars at centre of attention

England centre Seb Atkinson is attracting interest across the PREM as he approaches the end of his contract with Gloucester.

The 24-year-old has established himself in Steve Borthwick’s international plans but is yet to commit his club future as the Cherry and Whites get to grips with a new coaching set-up.

Atkinson’s girlfriend, Siena, is based in London, where she works for Goldman Sachs.

Depending on the development of No12s Bryn Bradley and Olly Hartley, Harlequins and Saracens could both emerge as potential suitors in the capital city.

Atkinson is not the only English centre looking at his future options. Max Ojomoh and Ollie Lawrence are both up for renewal at Bath, where Scotland’s Cameron Redpath is also reaching the end of his deal. All three could attract interest from France.

Exeter’s Henry Slade must also decide if he wants to activate an extension clause on his deal at Sandy Park. ‘Henry’s got a plus one option on his contract so those negotiations will start fairly soon because it’s time dated,’ revealed Exeter coach Rob Baxter.

England centre Seb Atkinson is attracting interest across the PREM as he approaches the end of his contract with Gloucester

Fellow England centre Ollie Lawrence is also out of contract at the end of the season

Who broke the sofa?

In a recent interview on For the Love of Rugby, Sale co-owner Michelle Orange was asked about rumours that a high-profile transfer target broke her sofa last year.

‘Within rugby circles, there are rumours that you didn’t sign him because he broke your sofa,’ said former England scrum-half Ben Youngs.

‘He didn’t actually break it,’ replied Orange. ‘We’ve got quite low-profile sofas in our lounge. Sometimes you slump onto it and there’s a big crack.’

Daily Mail Sport can reveal the player in question was 21st 4lb Bath and England prop Will Stuart – who subsequently extended his contract with Bath.

Curry's not for Sale

Sale want to extend Tom Curry’s contract beyond the World Cup.

Alex Sanderson wants the England flanker to remain in Manchester, along with a core of other out-of-contract Sharks players. Curry has suffered a series of injuries but that has not deterred Sale from offering a new deal.

‘I don’t want to let the cat out of the bag but Tom’s one of the lads we’ve talked to,’ Sanderson told Daily Mail Sport. ‘Tom, Bevan Rodd, Luke Cowan-Dickie, Joe Carpenter, Tom Roebuck, Nathan Jibulu. Cohesion is king.

‘Five years ago, when I came in at the start of a new season. I was talking to AJ MacGinty in the middle of September thinking, “I’ve got until Christmas here”, but by that point he had already signed for Bristol. It was a shock to me. That was a bit of a wake-up call. You’ve got to get onto these lads early because as soon as they’re out of contract they will have agents talking and other lads approaching them.’

Sale want to extend Tom Curry’s contract beyond the World Cup

Itoje committed to Sarries

England skipper Maro Itoje has revealed his plans to stay with Saracens beyond the World Cup.

The lock signed a secretive ‘long-term’ contract in 2024 but details of the arrangement were kept private. Itoje previously courted interest from Racing 92 but he told Daily Mail Sport that he remains committed to playing in England, so that he can continue to play for the national team.

‘I’m contracted until after the World Cup,’ said Itoje. ‘After the next World Cup, I still want to play rugby. How that looks, I don’t know yet. Ideally I’d love to play for England as long as possible.’

Quade on the radar

Australian veteran Quade Cooper has declared himself available if any clubs need to reinforce their No10 options.

The 38-year-old has not played since 2025 but he recently revealed his ambitions to make a comeback for next year’s World Cup: ‘It’s a home World Cup and I know I can still play.'

Daily Mail Sport understands Cooper has been added to injury-cover recruitment databases around Europe.

Australian veteran Quade Cooper has declared himself available if any clubs need to reinforce their No10 options

Sinckler's wages need to sink

Prop Kyle Sinckler will have to take a sizeable pay cut if he wants to return from Toulon to pursue his World Cup ambitions.

The Top14 club are keen for the tighthead prop to stay in France but that would rule him out of contention for next year’s World Cup. England could do with experienced props and Sinckler has played 68 times for his country, including in two World Cups.

Newcastle Red Bulls would have the financial firepower to sign Sinckler but they already have Elliot Millar Mills and James Harper on long-term deals.

With Josh Iosefa-Scott out of contract at Exeter, the West Country club could emerge as contenders with the backing of their new investors.

Saints want to keep dynamic duo

Northampton director of rugby Phil Dowson believes he can find a solution to keep both Archie McParland and Alex Mitchell at Franklin’s Gardens.

Both scrum-halves are pushing to become England’s starting No9, while also competing for selection at club level. Mitchell has a long-term contract and McParland, whose value rocketed while Mitchell was injured last season, is out of contract next summer.

Alex Mitchell has a long-term contract at Northampton and they are keen to keep him

But Archie McParland (left), who starred in Mitchell's absence last season, is another hot prospect - though his contract has only a year to run

‘Archie wants to play and Mitch wants to play and that’s a great position to be in,’ Dowson told Daily Mail Sport. ‘Is there enough rugby for both of them? I believe so, if we’re talking about things like game limits. I believe they can continue to push each other and we’re hopeful we can keep both of them. If you’ve got any cash, let me know!’

Tigers eye new Chessum deal

Leicester Tigers have made it a priority to extend Ollie Chessum’s contract at Welford Road.

The lock, who has 38 England caps and has become a potential future captain of his country, can command a hefty pay rise and the Tigers can ill-afford to lose another enforcer after George Martin joined Saracens last summer.

Jack van Poortvliet, Billy Searle, Joaquin Moro and Ollie Hassell-Collins are also among the players looking to renegotiate with the club.

Sports.title: Rangers clinch double deadline-day deal by landing Kevin Kelsy and Badredine Bouanani
Sports.content:
Rangers clinch double deadline-day deal by landing Kevin Kelsy and Badredine Bouanani

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Rangers have completed a double deadline day swoop by signing Kevin Kelsy and Badredine Bouanani.

Kelsy was identified as a priority target when Youssef Chermiti sustained a serious knee injury against Hibernian last month.

The Venezuelan international forward has cost the Ibrox club £9.2million from MLS side Portland Timbers and has signed a four-year deal with an option of a fifth.

The 22-year-old gives manager Derek McInnes another option up front to compete with Lawrence Shankland, Ryan Naderi and Bojan Miovski.

The fee is the second highest in Rangers’ history, second only to the £12m spent on Tore Andre Flo in 2000.

Kelsy came through the ranks of Mineros de Guayana in his home country then moved to Uruguayan outfit Boston River for a short spell before joining Shakhtar Donetsk in January, 2023.

Rangers unveiled the £9million signing of striker Kevin Kelsy from Portland Timbers

The Ibrox club also secured the loan addition of Algerian Badredine Bouanani from Stuttgart

He then joined Portland Timbers in January 2025 after a loan spell at FC Cincinnati.

‘I’ve heard a lot about the club,’ he said. ‘Even when I was younger, I saw the team in Europe. I know what the club means to the fans.

‘I would love to bring some joy to the fans and the club, and score goals to bring amazing moments to the team.

‘I know we have to win all the games and play well, and I’ll be ready for this with my teammates. I’m ready for this new chapter in my life.’

Boss Derek McInnes said: ‘We’re really pleased to welcome Kevin to the club. He’s an exciting player with a lot of attributes, and what really stood out in our conversations is how hungry he is to make an impact.

‘He’ll bring real quality to an area of the pitch we have been keen to strengthen, and his arrival gives us another exciting option going forward.

‘Kevin has a great attitude and a real desire to improve, and we’re looking forward to seeing what he can bring at Rangers.’

Bouanani, 21, has arrived on a year’s loan from Stuttgart, where he operated on the right wing.

The Algerian moved to Germany from Nice in 2025 having played and scored against Rangers for the French club in a European match.

The pair’s arrivals mean Rangers have signed 14 players in this window — either permanently or on loan.

Thelo Aasgaard has gone in the other direction after moving on loan to Anderlecht, while Nico Raskin is staying at the club after Rangers turned down a second bid from Turkish side Besiktas.

Sports.title: US Open reporter labeled a 'joke' by Aryna Sabalenka claims tennis star texted him to apologize after furious press conference tirade
Sports.content:
US Open reporter labeled a 'joke' by Aryna Sabalenka claims tennis star texted him to apologize after furious press conference tirade

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Aryna Sabalenka and her agent apologized via text message after a heated press conference exchange, the reporter involved has claimed.

Sabalenka was involved in a heated moment after her US Open second round win over Polina Iatcenko when she took issue with a question from Matthew Futterman of the New York Times-owned website, The Athletic.

Futterman asked the Belarusian about her sponsor obligations in the run-up to the tournament. She was spotted at a host of events in New York including for Gucci and luxury jewelry store Material Good.

'How are you finding your mood now that the tournament has started?' asked Futterman. 'Obviously last week it's lots of parties and fun and stuff like that.'

But Sabalenka groaned in response, responding: 'You guys are like a joke. Parties? Fun? Why would you even say that?

'Why would you even think about that? Like, what kind of question is that? Just because I posted some activities with brands and you think that I've been partying?'

Aryna Sabalenka had a spiky exchange in her most recent US Open press conference

Matt Futterman says he received a text apologizing from Sabalenka and her agent

Futterman quickly clarified: 'For everyone who is unclear, I'm not suggesting that Aryna is having fun at these parties. I'm saying that she makes a lot of appearances and there's a lot to do and lots of events, okay?'.

But Sabalenka insisted he 'move on', then finally answered the question: 'Oh, yeah, I wasn't serious before that. Next question.'

As the next reporter began their question, she fired one last dig at Futterman, saying: 'Think before you say stuff.'

The incident has sparked a massive debate, but Futterman has responded to a fan on social media who claimed he was 'cooked' by Sabalenka in a reply to his article about her bid for a third straight US Open title.

'She and her agent actually texted me to apologize, which I appreciated,' Futterman claimed.

Sabalenka had already had one spiky exchange over her off-court commitments after her first-round match.

'What is the question there?', she interjected during a question about balancing her energy with off-court commitments and practice.

She questioned: 'Why do you think that the week before wasn't focused on tennis?

Sabalenka was playing her second round match at Arthur Ashe Stadium on Wednesday night

Sabalenka progressed against Polina Iatcenko to keep her three-peat bid alive in New York

'It's like my hobby outside of tennis, the whole schedule we plan is all around tennis, so all of those events is not drawing me in any way.

'And all people that I work, all brands that I work with, I choose them very carefully. I have to be really comfortable around those people just so in that case I'm not drawing my energy when I'm surrounded by them. So I'm really enjoying my time with my brands, with people who works there.

'I have fun. It's like my hobby outside of my tennis schedule, and it actually gives me so much energy.'

Sabalenka is bidding to become the first woman since Serena Williams 12 years ago to win three straight US Open women's singles titles. She is back in action on Friday against Kamilla Rakhimova.

Sports.title: Fuming ex-Man City star Leroy Sane tells Galatasaray chiefs he is 'unhappy' in crunch talks after being DROPPED as German star's struggles in Turkey continue
Sports.content:
It is anything but Turkish delight for former Manchester City and Bayern Munich star Leroy Sane, amid reports that he is unhappy with his role at Galatasaray. According to Turkish newspaper Sabah, the 30-year-old winger has made it known to club officials that he is displeased at his lack of playing time. They add that he does not see himself as someone who will only make cameos for the club. Sane was named in their starting XI for their season-opening 2-2 home draw with 10-man Corum on August 14 but has since been dropped to the bench for their following two matches - with Yunus Akgun taking his spot. He came off the bench on 65 minutes during a 4-0 win at Erzurumspor - with Gala already 3-0 ahead - on August 21. Then in Saturday's 3-2 win over Goztepe he came on with 17 minutes remaining in the second half as the Turkish giants held on. Galatasaray sit top of the Turkish Super Lig ahead of Friday's trip to city rivals Istanbul Basaksehir but it is yet to be seen what role Sane will have. Leroy Sane is reportedly unhappy at his lack of playing time at Turkish giants Galatasaray Sane started their opening Turkish Super Lig match but has been dropped to the bench since Competition on the flanks will have only increased following Gala's recent purchase of Rafael Leao from AC Milan - although the Portugal international is primarily a left-winger, whereas Sane plays on the right. However, if Leao does start on the left on Friday then that could see regular starter Baris Alper Yilmaz move to the right wing, which would further hinder Sane's chances. Germany international Sane joined Galatasaray on a free transfer from Bayern Munich in June 2025 on a three-year contract - with the club announcing he will earn a guaranteed £7.66million a year, external plus a loyalty bonus. In his first season at the club, he won the Turkish Super Lig and Turkish Super Cup - scoring seven goals and providing nine assists in 43 appearances across all competitions.

Sports.title: Richarlison AXED from Tottenham's Premier League squad by Roberto De Zerbi: Wantaway star left out as he pushes to join Mo Salah in Turkey after Everton transfer saga and cryptic social media messages
Sports.content:
Tottenham have axed Richarlison from their Premier League squad but a proposed move to Trabzonspor has yet to be completed.

The Brazilian international forward, who has one year remaining on his Spurs contract with the option for another year, is a transfer target for the Turkish Super Lig club who shocked football earlier this summer by signing Mohamed Salah on a free transfer.

Turkey's transfer deadline is on Friday, and Richarlison is understood to be keen to make the move to link up with Salah and Fabinho, another former Liverpool favourite and a former Brazil team-mate.

Spurs however have yet to receive a bid they consider acceptable. They valued the 29-year-old at £35million in a deal set up with Everton for £65m Iliman Ndiaye last weekend.

Richarlison was told in advance of Tuesday's transfer deadline that he was not part of Roberto De Zerbi's plans for this season and could leave for the right price.

After omitting him from the squad beaten by Newcastle on Saturday, De Zerbi said the former Watford and Everton striker signed for £60m in 2022 had asked to leave 'too many times'.

Richarlison has been axed from Tottenham's Premier League squad as he seeks a move to Turkey

Roberto De Zerbi said on Saturday the former Watford and Everton striker had asked 'too many times' to leave

When Spurs confirmed their Premier League squad on Thursday, there was a place for Xavi Simons despite a serious knee injury which is expected to rule him out until next year, and for Dejan Kulusevski who has not played for 19 months since a serious knee operation but is back in training.

There is also a place for Wilson Odobert, also out with a serious knee injury, is also included although now classifies as a homegrown player.

Richarlison issued cryptic messages on his social media channels earlier this week as the possibility of a return to Everton emerged as part of a trade with Ndiaye, who ended up signing for Manchester City on deadline day.

The Brazilian posted a picture on Instagram of a slogan saying: 'I am the villain of many poorly told stories.'

He then added: 'If Spurs and Everton reach an agreement, I'll return to my beloved club. My intention was indeed to go back to the place where I was very happy. But the negotiations weren't going the way people wanted, and it won't be that way anymore. Despite all this turmoil, I have a contract with Spurs and I'll be available to the club'

Only after the English transfer deadline passed did the possibility of a move to Trabzonspor emerge.

Reports from Turkey claimed personal terms had been agreed with the player and that bids had been made, although Spurs rejected any such bids had been received.

By leaving him out of the squad, the pressure is back on Trabzonspor to strike a deal with Spurs.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia.
