World.title: New research: Bone deposits and plaque remember how ancient people lived
World.content:
New technologies make it possible to extract useful information even from deposits accumulated on bones or from dental calculus. Molecules deposited on human remains can provide a more detailed picture of how the plague spread across Europe, according to a doctoral thesis defended at the University of Tartu.

"The strength of ancient biomolecules is that they allow us to look beyond what is simply visible on the bones," said Biancamaria Bonucci, a junior research fellow in ancient DNA at the University of Tartu. Many diseases, for example, leave no traces on bones and can only be detected by studying ancient DNA and proteins. Written historical sources are also often incomplete and the presence of a particular disease in a certain region may only come to light through biomolecular research.

In her recently defended doctoral thesis, Bonucci studied ancient proteins and ancient DNA in a variety of materials. She paid particular attention to materials surrounding bones and teeth, including soil deposits accumulated on bones and dental calculus. "Soil actually contains a great deal of information about the skeleton, the individual and the burial environment. It can reveal stories that have remained hidden until now," Bonucci said.

Unwritten plague

Previous ancient DNA studies have focused primarily on the lives of individual people. The ancient DNA and proteins examined by Biancamaria Bonucci add a new layer to existing knowledge by providing context about the world surrounding ancient people. Ancient biomolecules can offer clues about what domestic animals people kept, what species they came into contact with, what diseases they suffered from and what the local climate was like during their lifetimes.

For example, one surprising finding in Bonucci's research was that a soil sample contained DNA from a lineage of black rats (Rattus rattus) that is now extinct in England. "What was important was that both the DNA and the proteins told the same story. In addition to the rat's genetic material, we found many proteins characteristic of that rat in the sediment. This allowed us to confirm that it was indeed this particular species, which is no longer found in England," Bonucci said.

Biancamaria Bonucci in the contamination-controlled ancient DNA laboratory at the University of Tartu sampling tiny amounts of soil for further analysis. Source: Biancamaria Bonucci

In another study, she used dental remains to investigate infectious diseases that afflicted residents of Sint-Truiden, a medieval and early modern town in what is now Belgium. The composition of the samples indicated that the hepatitis B virus and the louse-borne, fever-causing bacterium Borrelia recurrentis, among others, once circulated in the town. "What was remarkable was that we also found traces of the plague bacterium Yersinia pestis dating to the 14th century, even though it was not mentioned in any chronicles," Bonucci added.

While plague victims were typically buried in mass graves, in Sint-Truiden, signs of plague were found in people laid to rest in ordinary individual graves. "These people may have been infected but died so quickly that we simply don't know the exact circumstances. In any case, the finding was surprising and added a new piece of information to the historical record," Bonucci said.

In another case study, she and her colleagues examined Bronze Age remains from Grotta della Spinoza in Italy. "These were not conventional burials, but rather scattered human bones from which we extracted DNA," Bonucci explained.

The remains of one of the cave's occupants showed traces of several viruses as well as both HBV and plague. "This individual is the earliest known carrier of Yersinia pestis in Southern and Western Europe," Bonucci said. According to her, this further confirms that ancient DNA can provide valuable information about periods for which no written sources exist.

The finding also opens up avenues for further research as it is not known exactly how the plague bacterium spread so long ago. Today, it is transmitted by rats and fleas, but ancient strains of the bacterium lacked the genes that would have allowed them to spread via fleas. "We found the plague bacterium alongside the zoonotic bacterium Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae. We can therefore infer that they may have become infected through direct contact with animals, for example by eating meat from certain animals," Bonucci said.

Concretion-covered dentitions of three of the individuals on which one of the studies was focused on, with sampled region indicated in yellow. Source: Biancamaria Bonucci

Some finds should not be cleaned

According to Bonucci, her doctoral thesis had two aims: On the one hand, she demonstrated that ancient molecules are worth studying in materials originating outside the human body. On the other, she gained new insights into the history of specific archaeological sites. "Molecular studies give us much more information not only about the individual, but also about the environment that surrounded them and the diseases they likely suffered from," she said.

While the ability of teeth and bones to preserve DNA is well known, dental calculus and sediments accumulated on bones have received little previous study as repositories of information. Bonucci set out to fill that gap. "For example, we didn't find much human DNA in dental calculus. However, we did find a great deal of microbial DNA — specifically, DNA from the microbes that live in our mouths," she explained.

One study, however, showed that soil sediment covering a bone contained DNA from the same person as the bone itself. The exact origin of the sediment is unknown, but Bonucci believes it, too, forms after the body decomposes and preserves information in a similar way to dental calculus. "Unlike sediment, dental calculus forms during a person's lifetime and later fossilizes. It was very surprising that preservation in these two materials was so similar," she said.

In light of her doctoral research, she recommends that archaeologists avoid cleaning all material off finds during excavations. It is also worth preserving a certain amount of local soil and sediment. "I would recommend that archaeologists keep the soil and ask one of their geneticist friends to analyze it," Bonucci said.

According to Bonucci, the study's most striking findings — the extinct rat lineage in England and evidence of the plague bacterium's early spread in Europe — also indicate that the historical relationship between humans and animals deserves greater attention. "Based on ancient biomolecules, we can infer that many diseases in prehistoric times originated precisely from our closer contact with animals," she said.

She also urged researchers not to overlook ethical considerations when studying people and animals that died long ago. While research involving living people is subject to oversight by ethics committees, the situation is more complicated when it comes to ancient material. "Ancient material is a finite resource. We can't keep taking tooth and bone samples from these people indefinitely. We also need to understand that a person is more than just their body — we can find a person's DNA in the soil as well," Bonucci emphasized.

Graphical abstract of one of the studies included in the thesis. It shows the process of extraction of ancient biomolecules from concretions adhered to the skeleton and the results of the analysis. Source: Biancamaria Bonucci

Biancamaria Bonucci defended her doctoral thesis in gene technology, "Reading the archaeological record through ancient biomolecules: preservation, disease landscapes and human-microbe interactions in the past," at the University of Tartu on August 14. Her supervisors were Professor Kristiina Tambets and Antonio de Dios Martinez of the University of Tartu and Christiana Lyn Scheib of the University of Cambridge. The opponent was Associate Professor Camilla Speller of the University of British Columbia.

World.title: Government to discuss new defense minister candidates next week
World.content:
Prime Minister Kristen Michal has ruled out Reform Party Secretary General Kristo Enn Vaga as Estonia's next defense minister, saying the party will begin discussing candidates to replace Hanno Pevkur next week.

Although Reform Party Secretary General Kristo Enn Vaga has been mentioned in the media as a possible candidate for defense minister, Prime Minister Kristen Michal ruled out the possibility, saying the two roles are incompatible.

Michal said Vaga would continue as Reform Party secretary general and suggested he take the speculation as a compliment.

Vaga also said he was not in line to become defense minister. He thanked journalists, businesspeople and friends who had asked about the possibility, calling the speculation "a great honor and a vote of confidence."

Vaga said he would remain focused on his work as Reform Party secretary general until the elections while helping the party find a strong new defense minister. He said the next minister should continue strengthening Estonia's defense capabilities, ensure transparency over defense spending of more than 5 percent of GDP and maintain Estonia's unwavering support for Ukraine.

According to Michal, Reform Party members will begin discussing potential candidates next week. The new minister will be able to take the oath of office when parliament reconvenes the following week.

Michal also praised outgoing Defense Minister Hanno Pevkur for taking political responsibility, while stressing that this did not mean Pevkur was personally responsible for any wrongdoing.

"If, in the course of helping Ukraine, someone in his area of government took risks that should not have been taken and for which he is assuming political responsibility, that does not mean he bears personal responsibility," Michal said.

Pevkur announced Wednesday on ETV news show "Aktuaalne kaamera" that he was resigning as defense minister. He had held the post since 2022.

Prosecutors opened criminal proceedings Tuesday to investigate circumstances within the Ministry of Defense's area of government that were addressed in National Audit Office audits this year and last year. No one has been named as a suspect.

It emerged Wednesday that Estonia had sought to purchase artillery shells for Ukraine and paid €70 million in advance to Indian businesspeople who had reportedly never previously sold artillery shells.

World.title: Iraqi judiciary completes interrogation of 5,700 ISIS suspects
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Supreme Judicial Council of Iraq has officially concluded the interrogation process for 5,704 ISIS detainees who were moved from northeastern Syria earlier this year, preparing them for trial.

The First Karkh Investigation Court said in a statement on Tuesday that it concluded the investigation phase of one of Iraq’s largest terrorism-related cases in history.

The verified detainees originate from 67 different nationalities, including 3,497 Syrians and 474 Iraqis.

The courts identified very dangerous agents in key leadership, military, financial, media, and security roles inside ISIS.

Six offenders were actively linked to the captivity, detention, transfer, sale, and exploitation of Yazidi women, exposing serious international crimes.

Several suspects have previously been cleared and released due to insufficient evidence linking them to terrorism crimes.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate rises in Baghdad, remain stable in Erbil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar rose on Thursday in Baghdad, the Iraqi capital, and remained stable in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,547.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,546.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad rose, ranging between 1,552.5 Iraqi dinars and 1,542.5 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate remained stable, fluctuating between 1,546 and 1,545.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation represented more than a 10 percent difference in exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq exports fuel oil through Jordan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told Attaqa News that Iraq began exporting fuel oil shipments via Jordan for the first time last month.

Al-Rikabi explained that Iraq is exporting fuel oil through the neighboring country, not to Jordan.

The Iraqi official did not disclose the details of the agreement, its duration, or when it came into effect.

Iraqi oil shipments started flowing to Jordan in early August through the Trebil border crossing, the only land border crossing between the two countries, at a rate of 10,000 barrels per day, which were stored in the facilities of the Jordan Oil Terminals Company (JOTC), Jordan’s state-owned petroleum logistics and independent storage provider.

Through Jordan, a shipment totaling 307,000 barrels was exported to Greece.

Following the Strait of Hormuz crisis, which began with the United States’ war against Iran on February 28, Iraqi fuel oil shipments began transiting through Syria via tanker trucks, with storage at the Baniyas refinery before shipping to worldwide markets.

Between March and the end of August, Iraq exported 21.4 million barrels of fuel oil through Syria and only 307,000 barrels through Jordan.

Iraqi fuel oil exports started to increase following the Middle East conflict until the end of August in an attempt to compensate for the declining supplies via the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: 38 officers, 3,000 personnel dismissed over corruption in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Interior announced on Thursday that it permanently dismissed 38 officers and 180 personnel over administrative and financial corruption, with another 3,245 personnel discharged for desertion.

The purge represents a significant internal effort as part of the ongoing “Operation Dawn,” a nationwide anti-corruption campaign spearheaded by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government. The campaign has targeted numerous public officials and high-profile individuals.

According to an official statement from Miqdad Miri, the spokesperson for the Interior Ministry, the total number of individuals affected encompasses various categories of misconduct.

After receiving clear evidence of their direct involvement in bribery and financial misconduct, 38 officers were permanently removed from service.

Finalized judicial verdicts convicting 180 enlisted personnel of corruption accusations resulted in their official removal from service.

As part of larger ministry attempts to reestablish strong institutional discipline, 3,245 service personnel were discharged only for abandoning their duties.

These dismissals took place within the first 100 days of the current government’s tenure.

This security-sector cleanup is part of the larger nationwide drive “Operation Dawn.” Between late June and August, security operations resulted in the arrest of at least 210 lawmakers, public servants, and business executives.

World.title: Iraq, AIIB discuss financing development projects
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Finance Minister Faleh Sari met with a delegation from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) led by Konstantin Limitovskiy on Wednesday to discuss funding infrastructure and development projects in Iraq.

During their meeting in Baghdad, the AIIB delegation reviewed its global and regional portfolios to outline how its framework will apply to Iraq across the transportation, energy, water, and digital infrastructure sectors, according to a statement cited by the Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The discussions focused on the Development Road Project, Iraq’s mega-highway and rail corridor intended to connect the Gulf to Europe.

The AIIB publicly stated its willingness to fund and assist this important trans-regional corridor, acknowledging its enormous potential to drive economic diversification.

The Iraqi Ministry of Transport held separate discussions with the World Bank and the AIIB to determine the technological integrations necessary for the project’s ports and rail networks.

The AIIB delegation expressed its willingness to assist and fund important projects in Iraq, particularly major infrastructure projects, such as the Development Road project, which would boost the country’s economic development.

World.title: Iraq launches plan to recover 100,000 artifacts smuggled abroad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has launched a comprehensive plan to recover over 100,000 artifacts that were unearthed through illegal excavation and smuggled out of the country.

The Iraqi Ministry of Culture, Tourism, and Antiquities announced a broad endeavor to recover the country’s stolen Mesopotamian heritage using a combination of cultural diplomacy, security surveillance, and strong legal action.

The ministry’s undersecretary, Qasim al-Sudani, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the government’s agenda prioritizes the tourism sector.

The strategy emphasizes recovering documented items that were assigned official museum inventory numbers prior to their theft and smuggling, especially during the tumultuous period following the 2003 US-led invasion.

The initiative also seeks to tackle the significant number of unrecorded artifacts found during illegal and random excavations.

Since these items lack formal records, they pose a substantially more difficult legal issue to monitor and authenticate.

The Iraqi government has formed a combined domestic task force comprising the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Interior, the National Intelligence Service, and the National Security Service to carry out the plan.

Security agencies are cooperating with Iraqi embassies to identify stolen treasures that appear at public or private auctions abroad.

While countries like the United Kingdom and the United States have actively assisted in the return of tens of thousands of artifacts, Iraqi officials have indicated that some nations have intentionally delayed the repatriation process.

Iraq is also taking legal actions internationally against foreign businesses or individuals who are keeping Iraqi artifacts.

World.title: Iraq evaluates exploration blocks to optimize gas output
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil is actively assessing its exploration blocks and foreign alliances to maximize domestic gas output.

Director of the state-owned Midland Oil Company (MOC), Mohammed Yassin Hassan, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the ministry is focusing on unexploited exploration areas rather than existing resources.

The strategic measure seeks to attract multinational corporations to invest in Iraq’s growing natural gas sector.

Instead of altering production at current sites, the Oil Ministry is focusing on new exploration regions to identify new deposits.

Due to the strong interest in Iraq’s untapped energy potential, multinational energy businesses have already begun contacting the ministry.

Iraq’s MOC is actively pursuing partnerships with major US firms, such as ConocoPhillips, to lead gas development projects in important areas in the provinces of Diyala and Anbar.

Expanding operations in blocks such as the Akkas and Mansuriya gas fields is critical to Iraq’s long-term strategy for achieving energy independence and providing the necessary fuel for power plants to generate electricity.

World.title: Marsoumi: Iraq’s 10M bpd oil goal faces $75B cost and OPEC+ hurdles
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s strategic plan to scale crude oil production to 10 million barrels per day (bpd) by 2030 faces formidable structural, financial, and geopolitical hurdles, prominent Iraqi economic analyst Dr. Nabil Al-Marsoumi warned on Wednesday, September 2, 2026.

The assessment follows directives issued on Tuesday by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, who instructed the Ministry of Oil to expand exploration licensing rounds and ramp up extraction across fields in federal territory and the Kurdistan Region to target nearly 10 million bpd over the next four years.

Al-Marsoumi outlined four primary structural constraints standing between Iraq’s current production baseline and the 10-million-bpd horizon:

OPEC+ Baseline & Quota Negotiation: Iraq currently produces approximately 4.431 million bpd against an OPEC+ baseline allocation of 4.651 million bpd. Pushing production toward 10 million bpd requires formal revision of Iraq’s sovereign quota—a concession requiring consensus among major OPEC+ members.

Sustainable Capacity Ceiling: US petroleum consultancy DeGolyer and MacNaughton is actively auditing the maximum sustainable capacity across 19 OPEC+ nations. Preliminary assessments project Iraq’s sustainable 12-month ceiling at 5.0 to 5.5 million bpd, revealing a 4.5-million-bpd capacity deficit below the 2030 target.

Capital Expenditure Threshold ($75 Billion): Based on global industry benchmarks averaging $15 billion in capital investment per 1 million bpd of added capacity, Iraq must mobilize roughly $75 billion in upstream and midstream funding. This capital must finance seawater treatment and injection facilities, storage farm expansions, pumping stations, and new maritime and northern pipeline export corridors.

Price Collapse & Market Saturation Risks: Global oil absorption capacity remains constrained by demand growth projections. Injecting millions of additional Iraqi barrels risks igniting a market-share price war among producers, which could trigger a global oil price collapse harmful to Baghdad’s hydrocarbon-dependent treasury.

Comparative Analysis: Current Capacity vs. 2030 Target

Metric / Parameter Current Level (2026) 2030 Government Target Gap / Required Expansion Crude Output ~4.431 Million bpd 10.000 Million bpd +5.569 Million bpd Sustainable Ceiling 5.0 – 5.5 Million bpd 10.000 Million bpd +4.500 Million bpd OPEC+ Production Baseline 4.651 Million bpd Revised Allocation Required Requires OPEC+ Consensus Estimated Capital Outlay Baseline operational budget ~$75 Billion cumulative $15B per 1M bpd capacity Export Infrastructure Constrained southern/northern routes New northern & deepwater sea lines Major pipeline & storage expansion

Al-Marsoumi cautioned that upstream expansion cannot occur in isolation from global energy market fundamentals. Without substantial foreign direct investment to finance water injection schemes and deepwater export berths, aggressive target-setting risks outpacing actual midstream logistics.

Furthermore, aggressively pursuing volume over price discipline could depress international crude benchmarks, reducing net state oil revenues even as export volumes increase.

World.title: SC: BCI writ runs only over lawyers, not law students
World.content:
Supreme Court Thursday ruled that Bar Council of India has no jurisdiction to discipline or regulate law students

Only parent institution can take disciplinary action, says SC

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday ruled that Bar Council of India has no jurisdiction to discipline or regulate law students and quashed its letters threatening to debar Nalsar University law graduates from registering as advocates for opposing an invitation to CJI Surya Kant as chief guest at the institute's annual convocation.Despite BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra pleading for closure of the issue saying that the objectionable letters to the Hyderabad institute on Aug 13 were withdrawn within hours, a bench of CJI Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the ambit of BCI's powers, as the statutory regulatory body for the legal profession, is required to be delineated."From an in-depth consideration of the issue, we are of the opinion that Advocates Act, 1961, whereunder BCI is statutorily created, does not confer any express or implied power on BCI or state bar councils to take any disciplinary or punitive action against law students. BCI has disciplinary jurisdiction over law graduates only after they have registered as advocates," SC said.The bench agreed with senior advocate K Parameshwar who, for former Nalsar law graduate petitioners, argued that BCI does not have jurisdiction over law students, and its Aug 13 letters amounted to making deep inroads into freedom of speech and expression of students.So far as law students are concerned, it is the parent institution or the authority prescribed under laws and bylaws governing the institution who alone have the competence to take disciplinary action, if so required, against the students,â said the bench.Parameshwar said while the letter threatened to bar the registration of the Nalsar 2026 batch of law graduates as advocates, a second letter, while withdrawing the threat, directed the university to identify the students who had given the call to oppose the invitation to CJI as chief guest at the convocation. The advocate added that both letters were without jurisdiction.On Aug 14, SC stayed the operation of both letters, terming them âabsolutely uncalled forâ, and shielded the students and faculty ag-ainst any action by the university pursuant to BCIâs letters.BCI chief Mishra said that both letters were withdrawn subsequently.The CJI-led bench said, âHaving held so, we declare all the communications of Aug 13 or subsequent modified communications to be wi-thout any authority of law.âThis indictment and clipping of wings of BCI come a day after the same bench entertained petitions alleging serious irregularities in its functioning and its composition without proper elections.On Aug 14, the bench had also said BCI had nothing to do with the studentsâ protest against the invitation to CJI. âThe students might have written a letter to me. It is a dialogue between me and students. Who are they (BCI) to unnecessarily create an issue? This action is totally uncalled for,â CJI had said.Trashing BCIâs threat, CJI had told Parameshwar to convey to the students âto get licences to practice at the earliest and begin their careers in Supreme Court. We will empanel them and give them legal aid cases. This will be our response to all those who intend to create impediments in their professional career.â

World.title: Poverty, inequality seed delinquency in minors: SC
World.content:
The order stands in stark contrast to the lengthy judgement by a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Ujjal Bhuyan on July 21

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The full benefit of protective provisions of Juvenile Justice Act has not yet been extended to children who generally develop delinquent behaviour due to having grown up in poverty and environs marked by inequality, illiteracy and discrimination, Supreme Court has said.Exonerating a minor from the charge of attempt to erase evidence in a dowry death case, a bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Sh-ree Chandrashekhar traced in detail the history and development of JJ Act. They said because of industrialisation and urbanisation, rural folk migrated to cities and this weakened community cohesion, resulting in families losing control over their children.Writing the judgement, Justice Chandrashekhar said Wednesday, "Poverty, inequality, illiteracy and the discriminatory environment in which a child grows trigger delinquent behaviour... The rise in the number of cases coming to this court raising the plea of juvenility for the first time indicates in ample measure that there is a huge gap in understanding of the law by stakeholders."The order stands in stark contrast to the lengthy judgement by a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Ujjal Bhuyan on July 21 in the case 'X vs Bihar' where they held "today's children are exposed to complex information, graphic content and adult experience that were inaccessible to the previous generation".Writing the July 21 judgement, Justice Pardiwala had analysed what propelled a person to commit a crime - "It could be enmity, it could be poverty, it could be greed, it could be perversity in mind and many others..." But the bench had not mentioned inequality, illiteracy, or a discriminatory environment as grounds for a child to turn delinquent.The bench had further said, "There is no doubt that proliferation of technology and the pervasive influence of social media has altered the cognitive and psychological development of children. In such circumstances, courts as living institutions must be responsive to this reality.""The approach of courts or the juvenile justice boards dealing with a child in conflict with the law cannot remain stagnant since the legislation came to be enacted. It must bear a balanced approach towards the evolving nature of the juvenile and legitimate demands of society," Justices Pardiwala and Bhuyan had further said.Justices Mishra and Chandrashekhar said the prosecution's eagerness to bring the culprit to court and forgetting to assess the boy's age led to overlooking of JJ Act and violation of the rights of juveniles in conflict with the law."A child should not be treated as a criminal. He is a victim of the circumstances. Sometimes he is drawn to a world of crime due to socio-economic or emotional and psychological reasons. The state owes a responsibility to reintegrate juveniles in society, rather than permanently stigmatising them," Justice Chandrashekhar said.

World.title: Government to allow retrofit devices for polluting trucks & buses
World.content:
Govt will soon allow old polluting trucks and buses to be fitted with retrofit emission-control devices

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a fresh push to curb vehicular pollution, govt will soon allow old polluting trucks and buses to be fitted with retrofit emission-control devices (RECDs) that can reduce particulate matter emissions by up to 90% and nitrogen oxide emissions by 60%. Road transport minister Nitin Gadkari announced the measure Thursday, a move that will complement govt's scrappage and replacement programme for ageing heavy vehicles.Speaking at an event organised by Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (Siam), Gadkari said the device, developed from an innovation at IIT-Delhi, has been successfully tested. Once retrofitted in BS-IV, BS-III and older diesel vehicles, it can bring their emissions on a par with BS-VI standards. Similar devices have already been installed in diesel generator sets to reduce pollution. Gadkari said each device is expected to cost around Rs 4,000-5,000.TOI has learnt that to enable the rollout, road transport ministry will soon notify Automotive Industry Standard 228, which will prescribe technical requirements and performance standards for these devices.Gadkari also highlighted India's acute shortage of buses, saying the country has only two buses per 1,000 people, compared with the global benchmark of eight.He stressed the need for innovative public transport solutions in Tier-II, Tier-III and smaller cities, arguing that metro rail projects are often too capital-intensive to be viable in such places.Taking a swipe at bureaucratic resistance, Gadkari referred to the proposed flash-charging articulated bus system in Nagpur and said, "IAS officers think they are the only intelligent people in the country. Politicians may know only how to win elections, but they believe only they have knowledge.They keep creating hurdles, but it is my responsibility to resolve them."Gadkari also reiterated his ministry's plan to introduce a negative points system for traffic violations to crack down on habitual offenders. The proposal, which he announced Wednesday while launching the 'Suraksha' pilot programme for on-the-spot medical diagnosis and counselling of 10 lakh drivers, construction workers and other high-risk workers involved in highway and mining projects, will assign penalty points for every traffic violation. Drivers accumulating points beyond a specified threshold could face suspension or cancellation of their driving licences, he said.

World.title: 31-member parl panel set up to examine FCRA amendment bill
World.content:
JP MP Sanjay Jaiswal made chairperson

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Three weeks after Lok Sabha decided to send the contentious Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill to a parliamentary committee for scrutiny, Speaker Om Birla Thursday named 31 members of the panel, with BJP MP Sanjay Jaiswal made chairperson.BJP-led NDA's 19 MPs will be in the committee, while Congress has favoured members from minority communities as their representatives.Opposition parties, including DMK, which has split from the INDIA bloc, have been critical of the bill and supported concerns of Christian bodies that the bill's provisions will adversely impact NGOs run by them, a contention rejected by govt, even though it agreed to send the draft law for wider scrutiny to the panel to evolve a consensus.With many parties taking time in nominating their choices, the committee's constitution was held up. It has 21 members from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha, and was asked to submit its report by the last day of the first week of Parliament's winter session. However, a committee's tenure is often extended to allow it to engage in consultation with different stakeholders.NDA's members include Bhartruhari Mahtab, Nishikant Dubey and Tejasvi Surya of BJP, Sanjay Jha of JDU, Lavu Sri Krishna of TDP and Praful Patel of NCP.Congress MPs include Anto Antony, Viriato Fernandes, Hamdullah Sayeed and Christopher Manickam. DMK's P Wilson, a lawyer and vocal critic of the bill, is also its member besides NCP-SP's Supriya Sule and TMC's Kalyan Banerjee and Menaka Guruswamy, both lawyers.Critics' main argument against the amendment bill is that it allows the executive to take control of assets of an organisation if its FCRA license is withdrawn or not renewed.

World.title: To impart nationalistic learning, Bengal to have 1,000 RSS-run schools within a year: Suvendu
World.content:
KOLKATA: Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari set a target Thursday to establish at least 1,000 schools run by RSS's education wing Vidya Bharati in every district, municipality and panchayat within a year.

He also suggested a plan to merge the state's four education departments into one, specifying that there would be no separate administration for madrassa education.

Adhikari, who spoke at an event to mark the 74th anniversary of Vidya Bharati at Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture, urged the body to shoulder the responsibility of imparting what he termed "nationalistic learning". He invited its brass to the secretariat to meet officials and take the initiative forward.

Bengal has 313 such schools. Nationally, Vidya Bharati runs over 12,000 schools and 10,000 Bal Sanskar Kendras. The CM said he wanted the organisation to focus on establishing more schools in Murshidabad and South 24 Parganas, alleging that "more anti-national activities take place" in these districts. The erstwhile TMC govt, he said, polluted the education environment and institutions like Vidya Bharati would need to "help the state come out of this".





He accused TMC of even twisting the Bengali syllabus to divide people. "Mother was referred to as 'amma' and not 'ma'... The syllabus was created in such a way that Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar's or Swami Vivekananda's lessons remained neglected..."

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Invoking Syama Prasad Mookerjee's call of "ek desh, ek bidhan, ek nishan, ek pradhan", the CM said it would apply to education, too. "We won't allow an arrangement where the higher education department will look after all universities, while another department will look after Aliah University," he said.

Aliah University is currently managed by the state's minority affairs department. "I felicitated the board toppers.

Later, the minority affairs department sent a separate file containing the names of 27 Muslim students. I asked why? ... I have already felicitated 20 students, and they include Muslims, Jains and Buddhists."

Anand Rao, a Vidya Bharati official, told TOI its schools train students in "bharatiyatwa (Indianness)" as well as puja rituals. Some run till Class 5, others up to classes 8, 10 and 12.The website of Vidya Bharati Akhil Bhartiya Shiksha Sansthan states its vision is "to develop a system of education which would help build a younger generation committed to Hindutva and infused with patriotic fervour".

World.title: AIX crew member under scanner after handwriting probe
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Matching handwriting on a threat note found in the lav of a diverted Air India Express international flight with that of all 40 people on board has reportedly brought a crew member under the scanner of investigating agencies.

A passenger's role is also being probed. This Monday's Dammam-Delhi flight (IX 170) was diverted to Ahmedabad after a tissue paper with the words "bomb red 430" written on it and a box, both in black ink, drawn on it was found in the lav.

On landing in Ahmedabad, AI Express filed a complaint with the airport police, seeking a probe into who might have written the threat note. So apart from the normal protocol of checking passengers, aircraft and baggage, handwriting tests on all the 32 passengers, four cabin crew members and four pilots (airlines send extra crew to areas impacted by the US-Iran war to handle last-minute diversions).

"The agencies had asked the airline to give the same tissue paper for getting handwriting samples. Six tissues were sought for each passenger," said sources. AI Express arranged an alternate aircraft with new set of crew members that flew all the 32 passengers to Delhi on Monday-Tuesday midnight.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The crew members were asked to stay back for the probe. It is learnt that of them, seven were told Thursday they were free to leave the city.





"The role of a crew member is being examined apart from a passenger also being under the scanner," said sources. To be sure, no one has been conclusively found to have written the threat note and the probe is on.

An Air India Express spokesperson said: "We are aware that law enforcement agencies are investigating a security-related incident involving our flight operating from Dammam to Delhi on Aug 31, pursuant to a complaint filed by us. The airline is fully cooperating with the relevant agencies in the investigation. We unequivocally condemn any conduct that compromises or has the potential to compromise the safety and security of our guests, crew and operations.

Appropriate action will be taken based on the findings of the investigation."

World.title: Council can seek appraisals from teachers' institues: SC
World.content:
Supreme Court Thursday underscored the importance of the quality of teachers

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday underscored the importance of the quality of teachers, who play a vital role in shaping the future of the country, and held National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) can seek annual performance appraisal report (PAR) from teacher education institutions (TEIs).A bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe said the role of NCTE in ensuring quality education for children is immense and teacher education has assumed greater importance since right to education has been recognised as a fundamental right under Right to Education Act.The bench stressed that it is necessary for the council and its bodies to ensure accountability of educational institutions. It quashed the HC order which had found fault with the council's decision to seek PAR from TEIs. "We fail to understand how a regulatory measure of a statutory body, empowered to achieve planned and coordinated development of teacher education system in the country, could be restrained from calling upon TEIs to file PAR. ...it is but natural and incidental that NCTE would require the stakeholders to provide the necessary PAR," it said.

World.title: Home Secretary reviews Himalayan States’ preparedness for glacial lake outbursts
World.content:
Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan chaired a meeting with Himalayan States and Union Territories on Thursday (September 3, 2026), to review their preparedness to face Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) and snow avalanches, stressing the need for proactive monitoring, risk-informed planning, and stronger early warning systems.

The review meeting comes in the aftermath of the Nepal flash-floods which have claimed the lives of hundreds of people, while thousands remain missing.

The meeting was attended by the Chief Secretaries and State Disaster Management Authorities of Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, and Jammu & Kashmir, along with senior officials from the Ministry of Home Affairs, the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), the Central Water Commission (CWC), the India Meteorological Department (IMD), and the Defence Geoinformatics Research Establishment (DGRE).

Evolving threat

Officials reviewed the evolving threat posed by GLOFs in the Himalayan region, focusing on monitoring vulnerable glacial lakes and snow-covered areas, identifying high-risk zones, mapping potential flow paths, improving the dissemination of alerts, evacuation planning, and strengthening emergency response mechanisms, the MHA said.

The States and UTs presented their preparedness and mitigation measures, including monitoring of vulnerable glacial lakes, enhancement of early warning systems, last-mile communication of alerts, community awareness programmes, and deployment of response resources in hazard-prone areas. State-specific vulnerabilities and preparedness plans were also reviewed.

Mr. Mohan emphasised the need for continuous surveillance of vulnerable glacial lakes and avalanche-prone regions, particularly during periods of heightened risk, and called for close coordination among State agencies, district administrations, and scientific institutions to ensure timely action on warnings.

Focus on preventive mitigation

He said that preparedness efforts should move beyond a response-oriented approach and focus on preventive mitigation, risk reduction, and community-level readiness. The Home Secretary also urged States and UTs to regularly assess their preparedness plans, identify gaps in early warning and evacuation systems, and take corrective measures well in advance of any extreme event.

The Centre further asked States to expedite implementation of the GLOF mitigation projects sanctioned in 2024, and directed agencies to strengthen inter-agency coordination and regular sharing of risk information to minimise the loss of life and property in vulnerable Himalayan regions.

World.title: West Asia war LIVE: Iran media says six navy personnel killed in U.S. attacks
World.content:
Iran’s Tasnim news agency on Thursday (September 3, 2026) said six members of the Iranian Army’s naval forces were killed by U.S. attacks during renewed fighting this week. “The six died during a wave of U.S. attacks on Tuesday (September 1, 2026),” the report said, without specifying where they were killed.

“Seven people were killed in the southwestern province of Khuzestan, and four members of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard died in Kermanshah province,” Iranian media said. “Three paramilitaries were killed on Lavan island in the Gulf and another died in Fars province,” they said. It wasn’t immediately clear if the six naval personnel were among the seven already reported dead in Khuzestan.

Earlier in the day, Iran attacked U.S. military bases in Kuwait, despite President Donald Trump threatening further strikes in a fresh flare-up six months into the war. Mr. Trump said his military was prepared to attack Iran “any time we want” after extensive US bombardment of sites across the country left at least 19 Iranians dead.

Tehran retaliated by hitting U.S. military targets across West Asia, including in Kuwait, Jordan, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Iraq’s autonomous Kurdistan region.

World.title: On Uttam Kumar’s birth centenary, West Bengal CM vows to keep politics out of Tollywood
World.content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Thursday said the government will leave politics out of the Bengali film industry while launching the birth centenary celebrations of late actor Uttam Kumar.

“I assure you that the State government will not interfere in anything. There will be no politics. I want everything to be transparent. There is talent and I want that talent to receive proper nourishment,” Mr. Adhikari said while addressing one of the largest gatherings to celebrate the event at Tollygunge, home to the Bengali film industry.

At the event, organised next to one of the tallest statues of Uttam Kumar in the city, the CM said the Bengali film industry in its heyday was one of the best in the country. He added that renovation would be undertaken at institutions named after the actor as part of the celebrations.

Actor-turned-Trinamool Congress MP Dev (Deepak Adhikari); actors Prosenjit Chatterjee, Rituparna Sengupta, and Jeet; and director Haranath Chakraborty were among the top artistes present at the event.

During the tenure of the previous Trinamool Congress government, several artistes and the party were accused of “politicising” the Bengali film industry.

The government is holding a four-day celebration to commemorate the life and works of the actor popularly known as the ‘Mahanayak’ of Bengali cinema. Uttam Kumar was born on September 3, 1926 in north Kolkata and died aged 53 on July 24, 1980.

Kolkata was decked up on Thursday, with roads from the actor’s home to Tollygunge filled with murals, cut-outs, and cultural events to honour his contributions to the industry.

Some old single-screen cinema halls were also decked up as part of the celebrations. A stretch of the walls outside the Tollygunge metro station, also known as the Mahanayak Uttam Kumar station, was painted with graffiti highlighting the famous films and dialogues of the actor.

Mr. Adhikari also noted that Prime Minister Narendra Modi had paid tribute to the actor in a social media post. “Mahanayak Uttam Kumar... a legend whose timeless performances connect with people across generations. Tributes on his birth centenary,” Mr. Modi wrote on social media.

The Prime Minister had spoken about the late actor in his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ radio programme on August 30.

Film centre, stamp

Mr. Adhikari will lay the foundation stone for the Uttam Kumar Film Centre in New Town on Friday. India Post will also launch a special postage stamp commemorating the actor. The Uttam Kumar Film Festival will also kick-start at Nandan, with Nayak, Satyajit Ray’s celebrated 1966 movie starring Uttam Kumar.

World.title: Keeping pace with climate shock events
World.content:
Shaky social media visuals of the Rasuwa floods in Nepal have rattled the world. With over 1,250 lives lost so far — over 4,000 people are still missing — the extent of devastation is slowly becoming evident. Seeing colleagues in Nepal reporting from different locations and bringing to us fragments of information and various news angles was a stark reminder that the full story of a climate shock rarely fits into one dramatic headline.

We read about locals, tourists on holiday, and pilgrims. We see reports of governments’ outreach to help citizens, and assistance offered in rescue operations and contributions towards the herculean rehabilitation effort that awaits the country. We see social media posts from those seeking information about their missing loved ones.

While we share the risks of the growing climate crisis, each climate shock shows us that the world we live in is unequal and unfair. Soon after the flash floods, news outlets highlighted Nepal’s negligible contribution to climate change – accounting for 0.1% of total global greenhouse gas emissions. A point to ponder before we are drawn to unsubstantiated claims or conspiracy theories.

Reports of at least 900 workers believed to be trapped at 12 hydropower projects affected by flash floods in the districts of Rasuwa and Nuwakot brought back memories of Cyclone Ditwah that hit Sri Lanka late last year. Many of us reported from different affected areas. Each story, every life, was undoubtedly important, but the pattern that slowly emerged was hard to ignore. While the risks may have been common, vulnerabilities are different.

Among the most affected in this disaster were Sri Lanka’s Malaiyaha Tamil community, especially people working in the tea and rubber estates across the central and southern hill country. Historically marginalised, they not only contend with exploitation but are also the most vulnerable to climate shock, as Ditwah made evident.

The United Nations sought to mobilise $35 million in aid towards humanitarian assistance. The island is still rebuilding after the unprecedented floods and landslides. Some affected families stayed in temporary shelters for months, struggling to commute to the tea estates where they are employed for a daily wage. The concerns over compensation and transition to safe, permanent homes are far from gone. Ten months later, some communities tell us the cyclone is yet to pass.

Climate shock events of the magnitude witnessed in Nepal recently, or in Sri Lanka last year, draw global attention. But there are signs that show up from time to time. The stories may not be dramatic, but they are still telling.

In late 2018, districts across Sri Lanka’s Northern Province were severely hit by flash floods. Tens of thousands of people were affected; crops were damaged, and villages inundated. Neck-deep in work, the then government agent (a post similar to that of a District Collector in India) of Kilinochchi, who spared time to explain the situation to me, said: “In fact, we were giving drought relief to our people even days before the flood suddenly hit us.” As Sri Lanka prepares for the possible effects of El Niño this year, I am reminded of the GA’s matter-of-fact comment on how people and authorities were forced to combat one climate shock after another.

We have witnessed major climate shocks in quick succession in the region. The floods in Pakistan in 2022, floods in different parts of India over the last few years, the cyclone in Sri Lanka in 2025, and now, Nepal’s staggering floods. A Pakistani friend recently shared a 2009 piece from Himal Southasian on her social media. Authored by former diplomat Shyam Saran, it contended that South Asia is an ecologically interconnected system and called for a collaborative response to the climate crisis. Journalists in the region, however, have had more stories about natural disasters than collective strategies to tell.

World.title: Akash Anand in need of more political maturity, won’t give him key party roles, says BSP chief Mayawati
World.content:
Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati on Thursday said her nephew and party national coordinator Akash Anand needs to become more politically mature and decided against giving him any major responsibility in the party.

“I have allowed Akash Anand to work in the party, which is before all of you, but he still needs to become more mature. Till then, it would not be appropriate to give him a major responsibility in the party,” the BSP chief said while addressing a national-level meeting of party office-bearers in Lucknow.

The former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister also announced that her party will contest all elections across the country, however big or small, on its own.

Ms. Mayawati termed the Congress “strongly anti-Dalit and anti-Ambedkar” and alleged that Opposition parties are engaged in “misleading and misguiding” Dalits and other sections of the Bahujan society. She accused them of “favouring some Dalit groups and misleading people by making baseless claims and spreading false propaganda”.

She also dubbed demonstrations and road blockades as political and electoral gimmicks. “The BSP is the only Ambedkarite party in the country that is free from such political and electoral gimmicks. It is dedicated to the welfare and well-being of the entire society, especially the poor, labourers, exploited, oppressed, and neglected. The living proof of this is the development done by the BSP-led government in Uttar Pradesh for four terms,” she said.

World.title: BJP seeks sacking of two Ministers over Congress MLA’s allegation of corruption in Karnataka
World.content:
A recent letter to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar by Congress MLA Ashok Kumar Rai, accusing two engineers of Karnataka Rural Infrastructure Development Limited of collecting extra charges from contractors stating that it has to be given to the Dakshina Kannada district in-charge Minister and the department Minister, has now taken a serious turn with the BJP urging the Chief Minister to sack these two Ministers.

Addressing a press conference in Bengaluru on Wednesday, Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly R. Ashok urged the government to immediately dismiss the two Ministers who are allegedly taking bribes and also hand over the investigation to CBI.

In the letter, Mr. Rai has stated that an extra 7% of money is being collected from contractors in KRIDL, allegedly to be given to these Ministers and that contractors who questioned it are being threatened.

Mr. Ashok alleged that after the Congress came to power, officials were acting in an unruly manner and the government was running a “commission raj.”

“If ₹100 is released, only ₹30 worth of work is done. The remaining 70% goes as commission. When we made the allegation, they asked for documents. Now a Congress MLA himself has spoken about the commission,” he said.

It is estimated that around ₹800 crore may have been collected in the form of commission so far, he alleged.

Launching an attack at the Chief Minister for criticising the BJP’s padayatra, Mr. Ashok said it was “not political” and being taken out to create public awareness on issues such as drought relief.

World.title: Sixth day of Maratha Reservation protest: Supporters block major national highways
World.content:
As Maratha Quota activist Manoj Jarange Patil agreed to take IV fluids without breaking the fast, his supporters across the Marathwada region continue to stage “rasta-roko” protests, blocking major national highways.

The supporters are demonstrating to put pressure on the government to implement all the demands. Mr Jarange Patil’s hunger strike enters its sixth day, while head water and agreed to IV on Wednesday (September 2) in Jalna district’s Antarwali Sarati region. “I will continue to fast until the issues are resolved. I am giving two days to the government to act,” Mr Patil said.

According to police, the influx of people visiting Antarwali Sarati has been increasing. In the meantime, a bandh was announced in Jalna on Thursday (September 3) to extend support to the protest.

Similar bandhs have been observed in Beed and Dharashiv.

Besides, traffic on the Dhule-Solapur highway, Nanded-Bidar, and others was halted for some time. The rasta roko have been demonstrated on the Kalam-Latur road, Tuljapur- Hyderabad road in the Tirth region, and Indapur in Pune.

Several regions in Hingoli, including Shengaon, Jawala Bazar, Goregaon, Wasmat region, have been shut down. “Manoj Jarange Patil is fighting for us, for the community; if we don’t stand with him, who will? Government has been ignorant of our demands,” one of the protestors in Hingoli stated to a media person.

The commuters in a few regions were also affected as the supporters blocked bus movement at Dharashiv Kendriya Bus junction and a bike rally was conducted in Beed city’s Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj chowk.

Tension is flaring in the state, especially in Maratha community-dominated regions, as they are taking to the streets to extend their support. Mr Jarange Patil is protesting for the 11th time in the last three years. His fresh set of demands are the implementation of reservation based on the Hyderabad Gazette, Satara Gazette, immediate distribution of certificates based on the records of around 58 lakh Kunbis, validation of issued certificates, and others.

In the meantime, his demand for an extension of the Sandeep Shinde committee has been extended by a year till June 30, 2027, as per GR dated August 25.

World.title: Auto, taxi unions in Delhi seek fare hike amid rising CNG prices
World.content:
Several auto and taxi drivers’ unions held a protest outside the office of Delhi Transport Commissioner Niharika Rai on Rajpur Road on Thursday, demanding fare hikes amid rising CNG prices.

Five representatives were later allowed to meet officials amid police presence. “We told them that fares for taxis have not been increased for the past 15 years and urged them to revise the fare. We were told that a notification would be issued within 20 to 25 days,” said Anuj Kumar Rathore, vice president, Chaalak Shakti Union.

He added that if fare revision is not announced within 25 days, they will launch a wider agitation.

Haider Ali, the Delhi president of Aam Aadmi Auto Sangathan, said fares should be determined on the basis of transportation cost. “A transparent mechanism should be created for automatic revision of fares based on the rise of fuel prices. The expenditure of drivers has increased while the fares have remained the same despite multiple meetings,” he said.

World.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs2.84, HSD by Rs2.28 per litre
World.content:
The government on Thursday raised the price of petrol by Rs2.84 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.28 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs349 per litre while HSD will cost Rs374.31 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on September 4 (Friday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Loopholes fuel crime wave as illegal SIMs drive banking fraud, NA panel told
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Loopholes in the system continue to fuel a crime wave, with illegally issued SIMs being used in a large number of fraudulent calls and fake banking messages.

This was the grim picture presented to the National Assembly Standing Committee on Interior and Narcotics Control on Thursday, as regulators acknowledged that scammers remain active despite the blocking of 18.2 million illegal SIMs over the past two and a half years and fines imposed on telecom companies.

The committee was told that criminals were exploiting stolen fingerprints and “rented” bank accounts to carry out financial fraud, highlighting persistent gaps in the system despite ongoing efforts to curb the misuse of SIMs and banking channels.

The meeting, chaired by Raja Khurram Shahzad Nawaz, was attended by Minister of State Talal Chaudhry and lawmakers, including Anjum Aqeel Khan, Abdul Qadir Patel and Khawaja Izharul Hassan, among others.

Senior officers from the interior and law departments, the Capital Development Authority (CDA), National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), Federal Investigation Agency (FIA), Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) and Punjab Board of Revenue were also present.

NCCIA Director Irfanullah Khan told the panel that gaps in the current system were fuelling the surge in crime. Citing a recent raid in Multan, he said the agency had seized 195 active SIMs and 81 ATM cards that were being used by scammers.

“They are exploiting gaps to carry out their activities,” he explained.

PTA Chairman Major General (retd) Hafeezur Rehman admitted that the biometric system designed to secure SIM issuance was being bypassed. Fraudsters are now stealing fingerprint data from airports, driving licence centres, passport offices and possibly even Nadra itself.

In joint operations with the NCCIA, the PTA has raided 110 facilities, blocked 29,000 illegal SIMs and arrested 171 suspects. Data belonging to 600,000 individuals was also recovered.

State Minister Chaudhry observed that biometric verification had become “outdated” and urged a shift towards facial and iris recognition. He also called on telecom companies to upgrade their security features in coordination with the PTA.

He also flagged a new trend in which bank accounts were being rented out for laundering proceeds from scams.

Nawaz directed Interior Secretary Ahmad Raza Sarwar to urgently convene all stakeholders — including the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP), PTA, NCCIA and telecom operators — to devise a new plan to curb the supply of illegal SIMs used for online financial fraud.

The panel received a detailed briefing from the NCCIA, PTA, cellular mobile operators and representatives of the banking sector on fraudulent calls, illegal SIM issuance, misuse of biometric data and financial scams.

It also discussed emerging fraud methods, including unauthorised withdrawals and the use of rented or “mule” bank accounts.

Authorities were instructed to formulate practical legislative, regulatory and technical measures to strengthen Pakistan’s cybersecurity framework. They were also asked to raise public awareness about the unauthorised use of foreign SIMs and monitor social media to prevent their illegal promotion.

MNA Hassan suggested that citizens should receive an automatic SMS alert if more than one SIM was issued against their CNIC.

The PTA chief proposed that SIMs should be issued only through Nadra’s PAK ID system, while a SBP official recommended restricting each SIM to a single IMEI number.

In other business, the committee considered the ‘Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government (Amendment) Bill, 2026’ and recommended that it be passed by the National Assembly. PPP members Rafiullah and Patel recorded dissenting notes.

On law and order, Islamabad Police briefed the committee on the Safe City Project and narcotics. The panel called for anti-narcotics awareness campaigns in schools and universities, particularly against ice and other synthetic drugs, and directed that all Safe City cameras be made fully functional.

Last February, the FIA stated that illegal international SIMs, particularly those from the United Kingdom, are being widely used in Pakistan for serious crimes, including child pornography, kidnapping for ransom and online financial fraud.

Addressing a press conference, Additional Director General of the FIA Cybercrime Wing Waqaruddin Syed said that the cybercrime wing launched, for the first time, a crackdown on the unauthorised trade of illegal SIMs and as many as 44 suspects were arrested from Rawalpindi, Gujranwala, Peshawar, Sukkur and Abbottabad.

He said that a total of 8,363 international SIMs from the UK were recovered, adding that 21 cases were registered nationwide.

World.title: Woman injured in acid attack in Karachi’s Upper Gizri, police say
World.content:
KARACHI: A 35-year-old woman was injured in an acid attack in Karachi’s Upper Gizri area on Thursday, police said.

According to police, an unidentified person threw acid at the woman near Nasir Filter Plant in Upper Gizri, within the jurisdiction of Clifton police station, leaving her with burn injuries.

She was taken to the Burns Centre at Civil Hospital, Karachi, in an Edhi ambulance for treatment. Police said further investigation was underway.

Police surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed told Dawn that the woman had sustained burns over 15 per cent of her face, neck and abdomen.

Meanwhile, South Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIG) Syed Asad Raza said the woman’s husband lived in Punjab with another wife, while her three sons also lived with their father there.

According to the DIG, the woman worked at a bungalow in Clifton and was returning home in Upper Gizri when an unidentified suspect attacked her with acid.

“Police are trying to obtain CCTV footage to ascertain the possible identity of the attacker and determine the motive behind the attack,” he said.

Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar has taken “strict notice” of the acid attack on the woman and sought an immediate and detailed report from the South senior superintendent of police (SSP), according to a statement issued by his office.

The home minister directed police to use all available resources to ensure the immediate arrest of the suspect and take legal action to bring him to justice.

Lanjar also ordered an investigation into the incident and directed officials to ascertain the facts and bring them to light at the earliest, the statement said.

“He also directed the authorities to investigate the motive behind the attack and identify any individuals or elements involved in the incident,” it said, adding that the home minister had instructed officials to ensure that the victim received the best possible medical treatment and that all possible legal and administrative assistance was extended to her and her family.

Lanjar said a zero-tolerance policy should be adopted against those involved in serious crimes such as acid attacks, stressing that no negligence or delay in arresting the suspect would be tolerated.

“He directed the South SSP to personally supervise the investigation and keep him updated on its progress. He also instructed officials to ensure that all legal requirements for providing justice to the victim were completed promptly,” the statement said.

Earlier in June, 29-year-old Mahnoor Nasir was seriously injured at the Quetta Civil Hospital when another employee threw acid on her. The attacker, later identified by police as Humayun Shah, was said to have been kil­led in an encounter after law enforcers tra­ced him as he attempted to flee on a bus.

Meanwhile, Dr Nasir was shifted to Karachi after receiving initial treatment in Quetta.

In August, in a landmark judgement, the Supreme Court declared acid attacks more heinous than homicide, describing them as crimes that condemn victims to a “living death”.

World.title: Iran attacks US targets despite Trump threats
World.content:
Iran attacked US military bases in Kuwait on Thursday, despite US President Donald Trump threatening further strikes in a fresh flare-up six months into the war.

The new clashes, which began with US raids on Sunday, deepen the ongoing impasse in the war, as Iran maintains a stranglehold on the strategic Strait of Hormuz and the United States presses its counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

Trump said his military was prepared to attack Iran “any time we want” after extensive US bombardment of sites across the country left at least 19 Iranians dead between Tuesday and Wednesday.

Tehran has once again retaliated with strikes across the Middle East this week, saying it targeted US bases and forces in the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan and Iraq’s Kurdistan region.

Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei warned the US on Wednesday that Iran had adopted a “new strategy” in the war that “will shatter your foundations”.

Iran’s pummelling of US military targets across the region came after a US attack that hit a wedding in the country’s south, prompting fury from Tehran.

The Iranian Red Crescent said shrapnel from the missile attack in the coastal town of Kuhestak killed four people, including a child, and wounded more than 50.

The US military did not address the attack directly.

US Central Command (Centcom) spokesman Tim Hawkins claimed “the US military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC”, referring to Iran’s Revolutionary Guards.

Kuwait’s army on Thursday said it was intercepting a missile and drone attack from Iran, with the Iranian army saying it hit “the Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base in Kuwait with missiles and drones”.

Iran’s army also said it struck Al Minhad Air Base in the United Arab Emirates, but the Gulf country reported no such attack.

Kuwait called the attacks “a direct threat to its security and stability, and the safety of its citizens and residents on its territory, and a grave breach of the rules of international law”.

Aside from military action, Washington has vowed to choke Iran’s economy, threatening to slap sanctions on its trade partners.

Energy Secretary Chris Wright pledged on Wednesday that a US plan for expanded sanctions targeting the Islamic republic’s economic partners would deliver “absolutely maximum pressure”.

Trump also suggested on Wednesday renaming the Strait of Hormuz, a major shipping lane that Tehran has effectively shut for six months, as “Trump Strait” — although he implied later that he wasn’t serious.

“Now that we have it under USA control, should we change the name Hormuz Strait to TRUMP STRAIT???” the US president wrote on Truth Social.

‘Acts like Satan’

Iran’s top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf lashed out at Washington over the wedding attack, calling the United States “Satan”.

“If a power acts like Satan, picks targets like Satan, and kills like Satan, it’s Satan,” he posted on X.

Iranians meanwhile expressed dismay over the return to hostilities.

The war erupted on February 28 with US-Israeli attacks on Iran that killed its supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

A fragile ceasefire collapsed in July after attacks on commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, through which one-fifth of world oil supplies previously flowed.

Israel’s defence minister meanwhile said his country was prepared to respond “with great force” if attacked by Iran over the Jewish high holiday season, which begins in mid-September.

“For now, they are striking throughout the region except us,” Israel Katz said.

World.title: FIFA blasts UEFA 'smear campaign', fights World Cup plan disclosures
World.content:
FIFA has accused UEFA of a “smear campaign” and a “fishing expedition” after European football’s governing body asked US judges to force it to hand over documents related to its failed World Cup investor plan.

Global soccer body FIFA’s divisive plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to investors, unveiled in July, triggered a huge backlash across the sport, with UEFA threatening to boycott the World Cup unless the plan was scrapped.

While FIFA quickly aborted the plans in response to the backlash, UEFA is now preparing possible legal action against FIFA president Gianni Infantino for alleged “criminal mismanagement.”

Last week, it filed requests in three US states requesting the disclosure of documents related to the plan from FIFA and partners, including prospective lead investor Joshua Kushner’s Thrive Capital firm.

If successful in gaining access to the documents, UEFA had said it intends to lodge a legal complaint in Switzerland, saying it has been assured the case would meet the requirements to be heard in a Swiss court.

But FIFA has hit back, asking US judges for permission to contest the UEFA requests.

“While these applications are styled as legal pleadings with captions and docket numbers, they are little more than press releases in further support of UEFA’s smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership,” say the FIFA filings.

The filings, reviewed by AFP, say UEFA does not have the right to demand FIFA internal documents because no criminal proceedings yet exist in Switzerland or elsewhere.

Even if such proceedings did exist, the filings say, UEFA would not have legal standing because it has suffered no financial loss.

The FIFA filings also accuse UEFA of illegally bypassing Swiss courts but applying directly to US courts.

Disclosure of the documents, including correspondence involving Infantino and other named FIFA personnel and advisors, “would directly threaten FIFA’s interests and reveal sensitive and proprietary information,” say the filings.

UEFA has made no secret of its desire to remove Infantino, who had hoped to be re-elected unopposed for a fourth and final term next March after a highly successful World Cup.

UEFA may have been the harshest critic — it described his proposal as a “shady, opaque backroom deal” — but it has found solid support from North and Central America’s CONCACAF, and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC).

CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is widely seen as the likeliest challenger to Infantino – UEFA’s Aleksander Ceferin has ruled himself out.

The three confederations have kept up the pressure and collaborated on a no-holds-barred joint letter issued earlier last month.

“Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding — or demanding — power to be held,” they wrote.

UEFA added: “FIFA must once again be governed as an institution serving football – not operate as an instrument of individual power.”

FIFA has repeatedly disputed those claims.

“This application is yet another step in UEFA’s smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership,” summarizes one of the FIFA filings.

World.title: Estonian defence minister resigns after €70m Ukraine munitions scam by Indian company: report
World.content:
Estonian Defence Minister Hanno Pevkur has resigned following a scandal in which he authorised the payment of €70 million to an Indian company for artillery shells, only to receive ammunition of defective quality, it emerged on Thursday.

Britain’s The Telegraph reported on Monday that Datasel SRL was contracted to produce the shells for use by the Ukrainian military against Russia, and that Datasel had “not previously produced or sold a single shell”.

The newspaper says that Estonia made the payment from the EU military fund in August 2024 to send munitions to Ukraine’s front line by November that year.

“The Indian-run, Italy-based company repeatedly delayed delivery. When a shipment was eventually inspected in 2025, the rounds were found to be faulty and none were sent to Ukraine,” The Telegraph reported.

“The scandal is an embarrassment for Estonia, which has increased its military spending because it could be Nato’s first line of defence against a Russian attack.”

Pevkur announced that he would resign while appearing on an Estonian television programme, public broadcaster ERR reported on Wednesday. He stated that a leader should have the “stature and courage” to take responsibility, even if the fault is not theirs.

“As defence minister, I of course have to recognise that I am responsible for the entire area under my ministry, and if you are now waiting for that big answer, then, of course, a leader must have both the courage and the stature to take responsibility as a matter of political responsibility, even when there is no personal responsibility,” Pevkur was quoted as saying by ERR.

“I will take that responsibility and the prime minister will have to find a new defence minister.”

Pevkur added that he did not look at the contracts, but that his office received them. When asked why he did not read them, he replied that the defence minister “is not responsible for dealing with such details”, ERR added in its report.

“The defence minister does not conduct contract negotiations; the defence minister does not count socks and ammunition. The defence minister makes the fundamental decision to support Ukraine. The preparatory work for contract negotiations and finding contracting partners is RKIK’s responsibility,” he was quoted as saying.

RKIK, or the Centre for Defence Investments, is Estonia’s central procurement body.

Meanwhile, Datasel SRL is suing Estonia on the grounds that it delivered the bulk of the munitions — €59m worth — and would have met its obligations had Estonia not ended the contract, ERR said in a report today.

“Datasel is the party that has suffered losses in connection with these supply contracts,” the company told Estonian newspaper Eesti Ekspress through its lawyer.

“The actions of the Estonian Centre for Defence Investments, particularly the reasons given for the extraordinary termination of the contracts, are contradictory and illogical,” ERR reports citing the statement.

World.title: US extends Middle East deployments into 2027 as Iran conflict drags on
World.content:
